title.en: The sixth perek and renewal before Shavuos

summary.en: The Rav explains that the sixth perek is a baraisa added to Avos in the language of the Mishnah. He speaks of the time before Shavuos as one when a Jew can always begin anew, and notes that the parsha of Mattan Torah follows the parsha of Yisro.

title.en: Why the chachamim are named

summary.en: The Rav asks why the baraisa gives the names of the chachamim when there is no dispute. He answers that one who learns Torah lishmah becomes united with the Torah, like meat in a fire that becomes fire, so his name itself is Torah and mentioning it draws down blessing.

title.en: Chevron and Eretz Yisrael: the power of mentioning

summary.en: The Rav brings that in the Beis Hamikdash they announced the dawn by mentioning Chevron, to recall the Avos buried there, and asks why Moshe Rabbeinu mentions Eretz Yisrael so often. Merely mentioning a holy place or name, he explains, draws down kedushah.

title.en: The shoemaker who said the Rebbe's name

summary.en: The Rav tells of a simple chassid, a shoemaker, who constantly repeated his Rebbe's name with a wish for his health as he worked. He then speaks of the words of Torah as burning fire.

title.en: Mishnah as doubling: David's words to Naval

summary.en: On 'baruch shebachar bahem uvemishnasam', the Rav explains that 'mishnah' suggests doubling: tzaddikim say one thing with several meanings. He asks how David HaMelech could greet the wicked Naval with blessings, and answers that he was really speaking to the Ribono shel Olam, so it was not flattery.

title.en: Reb Naftali of Ropshitz and worldly talk

summary.en: The Rav tells a story of Reb Naftali of Ropshitz involving a request about milk, much of it unclear in the recording. He returns to 'shanu chachamim bilshon hamishnah': the chachamim could speak with people about ordinary things while their words were about far higher matters.

title.en: Torah lishmah and a story of a salvation

summary.en: The Rav begins the first mishnah, 'kol ha'osek baTorah lishmah', and speaks of each person learning according to his own path. He then tells a story, largely garbled, of a sick man whom the doctors could not help, a messenger sent to a Rebbe, and a salvation that came at that very time.

title.en: One Torah through different middos

summary.en: The Rav explains that each person receives the Torah according to his root and middah, as the Torah of Beis Shammai came through their middah. He compares it to water poured into glasses of different colors: the water looks different, yet it is the same water and the same Torah.

title.en: Lishmah, shelo lishmah and the rewards

summary.en: The Rav discusses Torah lishmah and shelo lishmah: each person learns according to his level, and from shelo lishmah one comes to lishmah, yet this is no reason to become lax. He goes through the rewards the mishnah lists for one who learns lishmah.

title.en: Refined things: wine, Kiddush and Olam Haba

summary.en: The Rav explains that the more refined a thing is, the more easily it is affected: wine becomes forbidden through a goy's touch, and some are careful even about his look, because wine is used for Kiddush and is likened to Olam Haba. He concludes that Olam Haba is so delicate that even a glance can affect it, and returns to learning lishmah.

catalogTitle: The Great קדושה of the מצה

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Pesach, the Yom Tov of Avraham Avinu, is the foundation of emunah, and that matzah, the 'food of emunah', carries within it the full holiness of Hashem's Name with which the Jews left Mitzrayim.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with Birkas haChamah, which will fall on Erev Pesach the following year, and with the dispute whether the world was created in Tishrei or in Nisan: Tishrei is din and thought, Nisan is chesed and deed, the month in which everything is renewed. He then matches the three Regalim to the Avos and shows that Pesach belongs to Avraham, the beginning of the Jewish people and of emunah; only Pesach carries kareis, because it is the bond with Hashem. The Zohar calls matzah the food of emunah, and eating it makes emunah part of a Jew. Through the foods of animals and of man he shows that bread holds all of creation, that lechem is three times Hashem's Name and matzah three times its filled-out form. He closes by urging care with matzah and chametz, which the Zohar calls the yetzer hara.

en: Pesach is the Yom Tov of Avraham Avinu, the beginning of the Jewish people; Shavuos and Sukkos are greater, but the beginning is the main thing.
Only Pesach carries the penalty of kareis, because Pesach is what binds a Jew to the Ribono shel Olam.
Emunah, the foundation of all mitzvos, comes from Avraham, and therefore the mitzvah of telling the children, the transmission of emunah, is on Pesach.
Matzah is the food of emunah; it is a mitzvah that is eaten and absorbed, so that emunah becomes part of a Jew.
Lechem equals three times Hashem's Name, while matzah equals three times its filled-out form, so matzah holds the Name in its fullness.
Chametz is the yetzer hara, which explains the great strictness about it and the search to remove it before Pesach.

kareis and the bond with Hashem

title.en: Birkas haChamah on Erev Pesach

summary.en: The Rav mentions the dispute whether the world was created in Tishrei or Nisan, and notes that next year Birkas haChamah, said once in 28 years, falls on Erev Pesach, when the sun returns to its place at creation. He adds that this coincidence happened only a few times in history, among them the year of Yetzias Mitzrayim.

title.en: Tishrei and Nisan: din and chesed

summary.en: The Rav ties Rabbi Eliezer's Tishrei to Beis Shammai's midas hadin and Rabbi Yehoshua's Nisan to Beis Hillel's chesed, bringing Rashi that creation was first planned with din and then joined with chesed. He then describes Nisan as the month of renewal: budding trees, new songs, the tradition that techiyas hameisim will be on Pesach, and its pleasant weather.

title.en: Pesach, the Yom Tov of Avraham Avinu

summary.en: The Rav matches Pesach, Shavuos and Sukkos to Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, lists the events of Avraham's life that happened on Pesach, and explains that Pesach, though not the highest Yom Tov, is the beginning and therefore the main thing. Only Pesach carries kareis, since it is the bond with Hashem, and an areil cannot bring the korban Pesach.

title.en: Matzah, the food of emunah

summary.en: The Rav explains that Avraham is yesod and emunah is the yesod of all mitzvos, so the mitzvah of telling the children is on Pesach, and the Zohar calls matzah the food of emunah. He raises the question how one can say 'Ha lachma anya' over a different matzah, and explains that matzah is a mitzvah one ingests, so emunah becomes part of a Jew.

title.en: Lechem, matzah and Hashem's Name

summary.en: The Rav shows that each animal eats food that matches its middah, while man, who contains all of creation, eats bread, which contains all ten. Lechem is three times Hashem's Name and matzah three times its filled-out form, so matzah carries the holiness with which the Jews left Mitzrayim, and therefore one can truly say 'Ha lachma anya'.

title.en: Care with matzah; chametz and the yetzer hara

summary.en: The Rav urges care with matzah, the bond with Hashem, brings Targum Yonasan that the Jews were carried to Yerushalayim to eat the korban Pesach, discusses machine and hand matzah, and asks for matzah baked with yiras Shamayim at least for the Seder. He then brings the Radbaz that chametz is the yetzer hara, tells of a tzaddik searching himself with a candle, and calls on the listeners to use the special year when Erev Pesach falls on Shabbos.

catalogTitle: פרקי אבות: פרק קנין תורה: גדלות הצדיקים' ביאור ענין תורה לשמה וגודל גן עדן של לומד תורה לשמה

oneLiner.en: On the opening Mishnah of Avos, the Rav traces the chain of the Torah from Moshe at Sinai to the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah and on to our own weak generation of 'broken luchos', explaining what each link teaches and how the Torah is held today.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with Avos 1:1 and explains why the Oral Torah could not be written: it is inscribed on the heart and mouth of the Jew, a private code of Hashem and His people. With the Bartenura he explains why Avos begins at Sinai, and reads 'from Sinai' as the lesson of humility of the lowest mountain, which made Moshe, and after him Yehoshua, the vessel for the Torah. He then follows the chain to the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah, who restored the praise 'the great, mighty and awesome' because they spoke for the Jewish people, the kallah, while the prophets spoke for Hashem. He describes our era after the recent churban as a time of silence and of 'broken luchos', with hidden leaders whom one finds by following the old footsteps, and ends with the three directives of the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah as the answer to the weakening of the generations.

en: The Oral Torah is written on the heart and mouth of the Jew who learns properly, so it cannot be put in writing or truly reached by the nations.
'Moshe received the Torah from Sinai' means through the humility of Sinai, the lowest mountain; Yehoshua merited to succeed Moshe for the same humility and devotion.

The Anshei Knesses HaGedolah spoke for Knesses Yisroel and opened the era of the Oral Torah, which flows from Jewish hearts; therefore they could restore praises of Hashem that the prophets had left out.
Our era is one of silence and of 'broken luchos': the task is to preserve what was received, not to create new things, and to hold on to the thread of the mesorah.
The three directives of the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah answer three ways the generations weaken: in Torah knowledge, in the number of learners, and in yiras Shamayim.

humility as the vessel for Torah
broken luchos and the last generations

title.en: Why the Oral Torah cannot be written

summary.en: The Rav opens with 'Moshe received the Torah from Sinai' and brings that Moshe wanted the Oral Torah written, but the nations would then claim to be Israel. He explains that the Oral Torah is written on the heart and mouth of the Jew, a secret code only a Jewish heart understands, so even in translation it is not theirs.

title.en: Received 'from Sinai': the lesson of humility

summary.en: With the Bartenura the Rav explains why Avos, which deals with middos, opens with Sinai. He reads 'from Sinai' as 'because of Sinai': Hashem chose the lowest mountain, and Moshe reasoned that as the humblest man he must receive the Torah. The name Chorev teaches that one who lives a life of luxury cannot be a vessel for Torah.

title.en: Why Yehoshua received the Torah

summary.en: The Rav explains that Yehoshua was not Moshe's greatest student, yet he merited to succeed him through humility, as Moshe saw when he renamed him. He links this to the days of Sefirah as days of humility before Kabbalas HaTorah, and describes how Yehoshua served Moshe and prepared the beis medrash, like the moon that has no light of its own.

title.en: Restoring 'the great, mighty and awesome'

summary.en: The Rav describes the eras of the Zekeinim, the Neviim and the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah, who 'restored the crown': prophets had dropped 'mighty' and 'awesome' when they saw the churban, and the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah put them back, since a lamb surviving among seventy wolves is itself Hashem's might. He adds that praise of Hashem must fit the time and the situation.

title.en: The Anshei Knesses HaGedolah speak for the kallah

summary.en: The Rav asks why they are called the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah and explains that with them the written Torah ended and the era of the Oral Torah began, Torah that flows from Jewish hearts. The prophets speak for Hashem, the chassan; the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah speak for Knesses Yisroel, the kallah, as in the Berditchever's reading of Pesach and Chag HaMatzos. So in galus they could proclaim the praise that the prophets had left out.

title.en: From 'received' to an era of silence

summary.en: The Rav explains why the Mishnah says Moshe 'received' and not that Hashem 'gave over' the Torah: no human can take over the infinite Torah, but Moshe gave over all of it to Yehoshua. He continues the chain through Tannaim, Amoraim, Geonim, Rishonim and Acharonim, and calls our time a new era of poverty and silence after a churban greater than earlier ones, a time to preserve rather than create.

title.en: The generation of broken luchos

summary.en: The Rav explains that the last words of the Torah allude to the broken luchos, and these are the last generations before Moshiach. Yet broken luchos also lie in the aron, and the chain from teacher to student cannot stop; hidden, small leaders are found by following, as Shir HaShirim says, the footsteps of the flock, those who keep the old ways, and not those who invent new ones.

title.en: Leaders chosen by people, and our deafness

summary.en: The Rav says that today's leaders are not luchos from heaven but are appointed by people, and gives the sign for the true ones: 'the words that were on the first luchos', no new paths. He recalls that in the Chofetz Chaim's time all of Klal Yisroel knew who its leaders were, and says that today the weakness is ours: we have become deaf and do not hear.

title.en: Holding the thread: today's might of Hashem

summary.en: The Rav compares the mesorah to pearls on a thread: today no pearls are seen, only the thread, and holding it is the lifeline. A Jew who still davens and learns while the wolves of the yetzer hara tear at his words is the 'might and awe' of Hashem today. He suggests that the number 120 of the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah reflects the twelve tribes, all of Klal Yisroel.

title.en: Three directives for weakening generations

summary.en: The Rav explains that from the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah on, each generation only 'receives' and grows weaker, so they gave three directives. Be deliberate in judgment, because the special siyata diShmaya of earlier poskim, seen in stories of the Chasam Sofer and Rabbi Akiva Eiger, is gone; raise many students because fewer learn; and make a fence because yiras Shamayim has weakened.

catalogTitle: הדרכה לקיץ לבחורים הנוסעים להרים: לראות הבורא בבריאתו' שלא לפרוק עול' להיות תמים' ולעבוד הקב"ה לשם שמים (שייכות לפרשת שלח)

oneLiner.en: Speaking to bochurim before they leave for the country in the summer, the Rav teaches that every person is Hashem's shliach and must not forget whose mission he is on: to see the Creator in His creation, to serve Him with temimus and truth away from politics, and to make Hashem beloved through fine middos.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the Chasam Sofer on why the meraglim failed although Moshe Rabbeinu sent them: according to Devarim the people asked for the mission, so the spies were the people's agents. Every person, he continues, is sent down by Hashem on a mission, and summer travel, which begins in the season of the meraglim, is a chance to repair their journey. Through the Ba'al Shem Tov, a story of Reb Shimon of Yaroslav and the angel's answer to Yaakov, he shows that the yetzer hara's task is to make a person forget his mission. In the country one should see Hashem's greatness in the stars and in nature. A second point is temimus and emes in the generation before Moshiach: avoiding politics and disputes, loving every Jew, davening warmly, and making Hashem beloved, with the story of a son-in-law who learned ten years for a cat.

en: Every person is a shliach whom Hashem sent down from Heaven to gather pearls of Torah and mitzvos in this world.
Hashem directs every journey, and a person often does not know the real purpose of his trip; bochurim going to the country must remember whose shliach they are.
In the country one can see the greatness of the Creator in the stars, in a stream and in a tree, and this contemplation is part of the mission.
A Jew must serve Hashem with temimus and emes, without politics, cleverness or involvement in disputes between groups.
One must make Hashem beloved to others through refined middos and warm davening, not through coarseness or provocation.

candidateTopics: emes in the generation before Moshiach

title.en: Why the meraglim failed

summary.en: The Rav asks why the meraglim failed if a shliach carries the power of the one who sent him and Moshe Rabbeinu sent them. He brings the Chasam Sofer: in Devarim the people asked for the mission, so the spies were really the people's agents, unlike Yehoshua's spies in the haftarah, who succeeded.

title.en: Every person is Hashem's shliach

summary.en: The Rav compares the soul sent down to this world to a diver gathering pearls from the sea bottom. Summer travel begins in the season of the meraglim's journey, and with the Ba'al Shem Tov on 'mei'Hashem mitzadei gever' he explains that Hashem sends a person to a place, like a man sent to Chicago to make a brachah on water that holds a spark he must repair.

title.en: The brandy without a brachah; whose shliach am I

summary.en: The Rav tells how Reb Shimon of Yaroslav told a customer that his father's soul was in the brandy he drank without a brachah on the yahrzeit. He applies it to the summer months: travel is a tikkun for the meraglim, and a person must ask whether he is Hashem's shliach or the yetzer hara's.

title.en: The angel's answer to Yaakov

summary.en: The Rav brings Yaakov's question to the angel, who is the yetzer hara, and Rashi that an angel's name is his mission. He pictures stopping people on 13th Avenue to ask what their mission is, and explains that the angel's 'why do you ask my name' is itself his mission: to make people never ask what their mission is.

title.en: Seeing the Creator in the country

summary.en: The Rav describes the country's opportunities: saying Tehillim by a stream, watching a sunrise, and looking at the stars as Yeshaya says. He describes the speed of light and stars whose light takes thousands of years to arrive, and how small a person feels, yet Hashem lowers Himself to watch over every creature. With the Maggid of Mezritch on 'melo ha'aretz kinyanecha' he says the whole world is full of ways to know Hashem.

title.en: Hakol yoducha and the false freedom of the country

summary.en: The Rav notes that on Shabbos one praises the Creation in 'Hakol yoducha', and tells how Reb Eizikel of Ziditchov's 'Hakol yoducha' in Sighet brought listeners to tears. He then attacks the common lie that the country is a time to be free of all restraint, mentions a bochur who took off his tzitzis to play ball, and notes that the parsha of the meraglim ends with tzitzis, the reminder of whose shliach one is.

title.en: Temimus and emes in the generation of the heels

summary.en: As a second point, the Rav teaches that a bochur must go with temimus, without tricks. He describes the generations as one body, from the dor hamidbar as the head to our generation as the heels, jokes about a 'convention of heels', and explains that the last word of Shema, emes, does not appear in the Torah's text because truth is missing before Moshiach, as the Gemara at the end of Sotah says.

title.en: The meraglim's politics

summary.en: The Rav links temimus to Yaakov, the man of truth, and warns against the politics that fill even the frum world. The whole sin of the meraglim was politics: as nesiim they feared new leaders in Eretz Yisroel, and he brings the Chiddushei HaRim on Korach that the generation before Moshiach faces the same test. He tells the bochurim not to get involved in disputes between groups and to hold on to truth even when it is hidden.

title.en: Loving every Jew, warm davening, making Hashem beloved

summary.en: The Rav asks the bochurim to love and respect Jews of every group and never speak or think disparagingly of them, and to daven warmly but not wildly, which sanctifies Hashem's Name. He explains 'yoshvei kranos' as people in the beis medrash who sit with horns, warns against provoking others in the name of chassidus, and explains 've'ahavta' as making Hashem beloved through refined middos.

title.en: Ten years of learning for a cat; parting words

summary.en: The Rav retells a story from Rabbi Feivel Mendlowitz about a son-in-law on kest who learned every night for ten years because he thought the noise in the attic was his father-in-law, and found at the end it was a family of cats; everything must be for Hashem. He closes by saying the country is for gathering strength and drawing close to Hashem, and wishes the bochurim success and that they meet again in joy.

title.en: L'chaim and niggun

summary.en: L'chaim, scattered talk and singing; the ASR holds almost no usable speech.

catalogTitle: הדרכה לקיץ לבחורים הנוסעים להרים: יש לנו שליחות ותכלית בכל מקום' ימים קשים אבל יכולים להגיע בהם למדרגות גבוהות (שייכות לפרשת בהעלותך)

oneLiner.en: The Rav teaches that every journey of a Jew, summer vacation included, is a shlichus from Hashem, and that the hard days of Tamuz and Av, born of the spies' journey, hide the light of Moshiach for one who travels with kabbalas ol malchus shamayim.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the idea that every Jewish soul is a letter in the Torah, found in a parsha that matches its mission, and that some souls belong to parshiyos of wandering and exile, which is itself a tikkun. Pesach Sheni and Vayehi binsoa, both written out of place in Behaaloscha, show this. Citing the Ba'al Shem Tov on 'mei'Hashem mitzadei gever konanu', he explains that each step is set from Above, so a bochur in the mountains is sent to make a specific brachah. The yetzer hara is especially active in vacation time, so one must take on more ol malchus shamayim there, as the Torah's 'masa'os' are journeys of galus. He links the summer travel season to the spies' forty days in Tamuz and Av, days that hide great light and the birth of Moshiach. He closes with seeing Hashem in creation, the story of Reb Feivel's davening, and the power of tefillah that saved Kalev and Yehoshua.

en: Every Jew, family and generation has its own shlichus, and every soul is a letter in a parsha of the Torah connected to it.
Following the Ba'al Shem Tov, the Rav teaches that a person's steps are fixed from Above, so every place he reaches holds a specific tikkun only he can do there.
Going to the country is no release from ol malchus shamayim; there the yetzer hara is stronger, so one must daven and learn better and accept more.
The travel season of Tamuz and Av corresponds to the spies' journey, and the Jewish people must repair that journey with their own.
The days of Tamuz and Av are hard, but they hide the light of Moshiach and are destined to become yomim tovim.
In the country one can see Hashem's creation clearly, and contemplating it should bring better davening and love of Hashem.

candidateTopics: Pesach Sheni and Vayehi binsoa out of place
the spies and the months of Tamuz and Av

title.en: Every soul a letter, every Jew a shlichus

summary.en: The Rav opens with Behaaloscha and Shelach, parshiyos of journeys, and explains that each soul is a letter in a parsha that matches it, with its own shlichus. Souls that need repair find themselves in parshiyos of wandering, since galus is a great tikkun, as with Kayin.

title.en: Two parshiyos written out of place

summary.en: The Rav shows that the parsha of Pesach Sheni was moved from the start of Bamidbar so as not to shame Israel, and that Vayehi binsoa, per the Gemara in Shabbos, is also out of place and will return to its place when Moshiach comes. Both are parshiyos of souls in exile, and the summer travel season that begins with these parshiyos is no coincidence.

title.en: Steps fixed from Above: the brachah in the mountains

summary.en: Bringing the Ba'al Shem Tov on 'mei'Hashem mitzadei gever konanu', the Rav explains that a bochur who makes a brachah on a berry or a drink from a stream in the mountains may be redeeming a soul that waited for him since creation. He tells of a tzaddik whose customer drank without a brachah on his father's yahrzeit, losing his father's soul's tikkun.

title.en: Clothing as ol malchus shamayim

summary.en: The Rav warns that the yetzer hara is inventive, bringing the Ya'aros Devash on why people began wearing black on Shabbos. He explains that clothing casts a light of malchus shamayim on a person, which is why one adds garments for davening, and that shedding clothes in the country symbolizes throwing off the yoke; yet the Aron goes along on every journey.

title.en: A shlichus needs mesiras nefesh; the masa'os of galus

summary.en: The Rav says one must be more careful in the country than at home, since a shlichus demands mesiras nefesh, as the Midrash contrasts Yehoshua's successful messengers with Moshe's spies. Through the Megaleh Amukos on 'Eleh masei', whose letters hint at the four exiles, he teaches that a Jew's journeys are journeys of galus, to be taken with kabbalas ol and not with a feeling of freedom.

title.en: Tamuz and Av: repairing the spies' journey

summary.en: The Rav notes that the masa'os are read with the tune of the Shirah and recalls the Spanish exiles leaving with music, teaching that galus is to be walked with bitachon and the guidance of the leaders. He explains that the world travels in Tamuz and Av because the spies' forty days fell then, and reads the order of the camps' travel, Gershon and Merari, then the flags of Reuven and Shimon, then Gad, as a map of these months that ends in consolation.

title.en: The parsha of scattering and Reb Shimshon's warning

summary.en: After a Chelm joke about the pazer cantillation note, the Rav points out that Behaaloscha is full of pazers, a parsha of scattering that prepares the people for Tamuz and Av. He brings Reb Shimshon of Ostropolia that the letters before 'anavim' in 'yemei bikurei anavim' spell the name of the Satan, which is why the spies fell in those days.

title.en: Adding the yud: hard days become holy

summary.en: The Rav explains Reb Shimshon's hint: the yud is missing, and where a Jew enters these days they become holy and will be the greatest yomim tovim, as Zechariah foretells. He adds that Moshe repaired Reuven, that Gad's count ending in fifty alludes to Eliyahu and the redemption, and that Hashem sends each one on a shlichus, to be like Yehoshua's messengers.

title.en: The two Ashreis and the forty-two journeys

summary.en: The Rav contrasts 'Ashrei yoshvei veisecha' with 'Ashrei temimei derech', whose chapter ends with a lost sheep: being a Jew is easier at home, but when Hashem sends one on a journey one goes, guarding Hashem's charge. He brings the Ba'al Shem Tov that every Jew passes through the forty-two journeys, warns of the pull of ballfields and pools, and says these days hold greater light.

title.en: Moshiach hidden in Tamuz and Av; grapes in the desert

summary.en: The Rav brings the Chasam Sofer that Boaz married Ruth on 17 Tamuz, the Midrash that Moshiach is born on Tisha B'Av, Aharon's 'chag laHashem machar', and the Kozhnitzer Maggid on 'bein hametzarim', to show that these days hide the light of Moshiach. Through Moshe's charge to take of the fruit and Hoshea's 'grapes in the desert', he explains that Hashem delights in a Jew who uses these days for His sake, while allowing exercise for health in measure, as the Rambam writes.

title.en: The spies' grapes as nesachim; the stars in the country

summary.en: The Rav brings a Midrash that the spies' cluster of grapes was used for nesachim, and Rashi that the parsha of nesachim comforted Israel after the spies, showing that the sin itself becomes the tikkun; Tamuz and Menachem Av, he adds, equal 'Melech HaMoshiach' in gematria. He then urges looking at the stars and sunsets in the country, as Yeshayahu says, and the Rambam's path to love of Hashem through contemplating creation, as Dovid HaMelech did.

title.en: Reb Feivel at the window; the tefillah that saved Kalev and Yehoshua

summary.en: The Rav tells how his rebbe Reb Feivel davened looking out the window and answered a critic that he was looking into Hashem's own writing, the world of Borchi Nafshi. He contrasts the city that hides Hashem's world with the country, where all creations sing shirah, then teaches that Kalev and Yehoshua were saved only through tefillah, and closes with a brachah for a summer of growth and for the fast days to become yomim tovim.

catalogTitle: Our Joy on Pesach "הללו עבדי ה' ולא עבדי פרעה"

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Pesach makes a Jew a servant of Hashem instead of Pharaoh, that Nisan is a month of renewal in which a person should become new with all of creation, and that matzah carries the hidden holiness of the geulah.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the aim of Pesach: to leave the servitude of Pharaoh and become servants of the Ribono shel Olam with love and joy. The days before Rosh Chodesh Nisan are like the kohanim's seven days of initiation, so they are days of simcha. He explains the special seudah of Rosh Chodesh and Melaveh Malkah as seudos of Dovid HaMelech, and Maariv and Tikkun Chatzos as higher tefillos. Nisan is the month of Yehudah, malchus and Moshiach; the Shelah says the whole month holds the holiness of Rosh Chodesh. The world was created in Nisan, and every spring creation renews itself and sings; a person should join it and become new. He then turns to matzah: bread equals three times the Name of Hashem, matzah three times its filled-out form, which equals adam. The matzah we eat is the same matzah of the geulah, and he closes with a tzaddik's joy after the Seder.

en: The aim of Pesach is to stop being servants of Pharaoh and become servants of the Ribono shel Olam with love and joy.
The seven days before Rosh Chodesh Nisan are like the kohanim's days of miluim, days of initiation and simcha, so Tachanun is not said.
Nisan is the month of Yehudah, of malchus and of Moshiach, and according to the Shelah the whole month carries the holiness of Rosh Chodesh.
Since the world was created in Nisan, each year nature renews itself and sings, and a person should renew himself along with it.
Lechem equals three times the Name Havayah, while matzah equals three times its filled-out form of 45, the number of adam.
The matzah we eat is the same matzah our forefathers ate, because its inner content is the geulah and the physical matzah is only its envelope.

candidateTopics: pesach as becoming servants of Hashem

title.en: Servants of Hashem, not of Pharaoh

summary.en: The Rav opens with Shabbos HaChodesh and the aim of Pesach, to leave the servitude of Mitzrayim and become servants of the Ribono shel Olam with love and joy. He compares the days before Rosh Chodesh Nisan to the kohanim's seven days of miluim, which is why they are days of simcha without Tachanun.

title.en: Rosh Chodesh, Melaveh Malkah and Dovid HaMelech

summary.en: The Rav brings the short siman in Shulchan Aruch that it is a mitzvah to add to the seudah on Rosh Chodesh, alongside Melaveh Malkah, and ties both to Dovid HaMelech and the renewal of the moon. He explains that Maariv was a reshus because it belongs to a higher level, and that Tikkun Chatzos is the tefillah of Dovid, matched by Melaveh Malkah as the fourth seudah.

title.en: Nisan, the month of Yehudah and Moshiach

summary.en: The Rav explains that each month belongs to a shevet according to the degalim, and Nisan belongs to Yehudah, the month of malchus and of Moshiach; this is why tzaddikim awaited Moshiach on Pesach and why the door is opened for Eliyahu. He brings the Shelah that all of Nisan holds the holiness of Rosh Chodesh, and the Avnei Nezer that an hour of avodah in Nisan equals a full day in another month.

title.en: Creation in Nisan and the renewal of nature

summary.en: The Rav brings the machlokes whether the world was created in Tishrei or Nisan and explains that Na'aseh adam was said on Rosh Chodesh Nisan. What happened on a date is etched into it and recurs, so the renewal in Shamayim filters down into this world, and he describes the spring: trees budding, birds returning, streams flowing again.

title.en: All of creation sings; a person should become new

summary.en: The Rav connects Nisan to the haftarah of the dry bones coming back to life and to the brachah made on a friend not seen for twelve months. He explains why morning is called tzafra and night ramsha, after the birds and the insects that sing, and says a Jew sings by day and by night. Every person, he says, should join the song of creation, renew himself and be a new person.

title.en: The piyutim of Mussaf and the Seder night

summary.en: The Rav mentions that he had planned to learn the piyutim of Mussaf of Parshas HaChodesh, which describe the renewal of nature in Nisan, but they are difficult and time does not allow. He repeats that a person should become new, and that the mitzvos of Nisan, above all the Seder, are the way to do so; the tzaddikim said the Seder sets the program for the whole year.

title.en: Ten utterances, white food and universal bread

summary.en: Turning to matzah, the Rav explains that the ten utterances of creation reappear, in reverse order, in the ten makkos and again in the ten dibros. He then explains that people choose food by their middah, chesed preferring sweet and white foods like wheat, milk and the mann, and gevurah spiced foods and wine, while bread is the one food all peoples eat; the Shulchan Aruch notes the ten words of Hamotzi.

title.en: Lechem, matzah and the geulah inside it

summary.en: The Rav explains that lechem equals three times the Name Havayah, which is the holiness that keeps the neshamah in the body, while matzah equals three times the filled-out Name of 45, the number of adam. He explains that the whole Seder is built on questions, and answers why one may say 'ha lachma anya': the inner geulah in the matzah is identical, and the flour and water are only an envelope. He closes with a tzaddik who wept for joy after the Seder over the holy names he had eaten.

catalogTitle: הדרכה לקיץ לבחורים הנוסעים להרים: שיחת פרידה - ברכות פרידה' לקדש שם שמים' להיות מעורב ונוח לבריות' לבנות ביהמ"ק ע"י אהבת חנם.

oneLiner.en: Parting from the bachurim before they leave for camp, the Rav blesses them and asks them to sanctify Hashem's name through good conduct with others, warm tefillah and small daily acts that help complete the Beis Hamikdash.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the custom of Chazal to bless one another when parting from the yeshiva, citing the brachos in Gemara Berachos, including the wish that no talmid of the group turn out badly. From there he turns to the bachurim's time in camp among others: a ben Torah is watched, and bad middos or making things hard for roommates is a chillul Hashem, while good conduct makes him an example. He warns against showing off and pride, with a play on the name Devorah (a bee). He asks them to strengthen Torah and tefillah daily, to come on time and daven warmly, since kiddush Hashem is the greatest thing and chillul Hashem the worst. He brings the Sanzer Rav's teaching that the Beis Hamikdash is nearly complete, so small acts of self-restraint finish it, and a story of Reb Yechezkel'e of Kuzmir about ahavas chinam on Tisha B'Av. He closes with daily chizuk, like vitamin C, and blessings.

en: Chazal's custom was to bless one another when parting, and the Rav applies their brachos to the bachurim leaving the yeshiva.
A ben Torah among others is watched, so bad middos or inconsiderate behavior is a chillul Hashem, while good conduct makes him an example for all.
Torah and tefillah need fresh chizuk every day, and a ben Torah should love rebuke and words of mussar.
Kiddush Hashem is the greatest thing there is, and its opposite, chillul Hashem, is not atoned even by Yom Kippur and suffering.
The Beis Hamikdash is nearly complete, and small acts of self-restraint, good learning and davening by each person help finish it.
Since the Beis Hamikdash was destroyed through sinas chinam, the main mourning today is ahavas chinam, doing a favor for another Jew.

daily chizuk in Torah and tefillah
building the Beis Hamikdash through small deeds

title.en: Chazal's blessings when parting

summary.en: The Rav takes leave of the bachurim, praising them, and explains that Chazal used to bless one another when leaving the yeshiva. He brings the brachos from Gemara Berachos, including the wish that no talmid of the group turn out like Achitofel, Doeg or Gechazi.

title.en: Kiddush Hashem among others in camp

summary.en: The Rav warns that a ben Torah who goes out among others is watched: anger, a mess in a shared room or mockery is a chillul Hashem, while good middos make him an example. He warns against showing off group pride and against haughtiness, with a play on Devorah, whose name means bee.

title.en: Daily chizuk in Torah and tefillah

summary.en: The Rav says Torah and tefillah need chizuk every day, that loving rebuke is one of the ways Torah is acquired, and asks the bachurim to come on time and daven warmly. Kiddush Hashem is the greatest thing, and chillul Hashem is not atoned even by Yom Kippur.

title.en: Small deeds finish the Beis Hamikdash

summary.en: The Rav brings the Sanzer Rav's teaching that the heavenly Beis Hamikdash is complete except for the paroches, and his answer why he did not make it himself. Today only the smallest details remain, so small acts of restraint, not shaming others and good learning and davening, build it.

title.en: Ahavas chinam and the closing brachah

summary.en: The Rav tells how Reb Yechezkel'e of Kuzmir sent a weeping chassid on Tisha B'Av to do a favor for a Jew, since the churban came through sinas chinam. He asks the bachurim to help and encourage others, compares chizuk to vitamin C that must be taken daily, and blesses them.

title.en: The old chassidim's parting song

summary.en: The Rav recalls how old Russian chassidim sang a niggun when parting from the Rebbe, about meeting again if Hashem grants life, followed by singing and poorly transcribed audio.

catalogTitle: הדרכה לקיץ לבחורים הנוסעים להרים: להיות חלק מבריאה לעשות רצונו דרוש בפרק ר' אליעזר דמילה' נחיצות העבודה במחנה קיץ' חיזוק הרמת הקול בתפילה.

oneLiner.en: Speaking to bachurim about to leave for a summer camp, the Rav explains that each of them is sent there as a shaliach of Hashem, like all of creation, and tells them to fulfill that mission by learning, avoiding machlokes, and davening warmly and aloud.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the summer months, when the meraglim went out, and says that every bachur going to camp is a shaliach meant to repair that sin. In the country one sees how trees, birds and water all do exactly what Hashem commanded at creation; a person should join this 'family' of creation, but by his own choice. He warns against machlokes, citing Korach, and contrasts it with machlokes for the sake of Heaven. He then introduces the perek of Rabbi Eliezer d'Milah: through the Eglei Tal and Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer he shows that milah and Shabbos are one matter, which is why hilchos milah are taught inside Maseches Shabbos. He stresses the danger that comes with a great mission, and closes with a long call, from the Ramban, the Ba'al haTanya and others, to daven together, with warmth and a raised voice.

en: Each bachur going to camp is a shaliach sent by Hashem, and the place, the rebbeim, the chaverim and the learning are the tools of that mission.
All of nature carries out the command Hashem gave it at creation; a person is asked to do the same, but through his own free choice.
Milah and Shabbos are one matter, each containing the whole Torah, so the laws of milah are taught within Maseches Shabbos.
The greater the mission, the greater the danger along the way, so one must strengthen oneself and guard against lashon hara, leitzanus and machlokes.
Davening aloud is a proclamation that we are Hashem's creations, and the voice arouses the heart, so the Rav urges davening warmly and together, word by word.
Every tefillah is a diamond, as precious as Ne'ilah of Yom Kippur, and one who feels the pain cries out.

title.en: Going to camp as a shaliach

summary.en: The Rav ties the summer to the time the meraglim set out, and says each bachur leaving home for camp is a shaliach meant to repair their sin. The rebbeim, chaverim, learning and davening are the tools of the mission, and at every step one chooses whether to be a faithful shaliach or like the meraglim.

title.en: All of creation does its shlichus

summary.en: In the country one sees the sky, grass, birds and water without buildings hiding them, each doing what Hashem commanded at creation. The Rav asks why a person should be different, and says the bachurim should join this 'family of nature' as shluchim, but by choice, and work together as a team.

title.en: Korach and machlokes for Heaven's sake

summary.en: From Parshas Korach the Rav teaches that one may not make machlokes like Korach and his company. He explains that their dispute was split inside as well, each wanting something else, because each sought himself; a machlokes of Torah for Heaven's sake instead brings friendship and team-work.

title.en: The Eglei Tal: Shabbos, milah and the Shach

summary.en: Introducing the perek of Rabbi Eliezer d'Milah, the Rav brings the Eglei Tal's introduction: he wrote on hilchos Shabbos as a tikkun for pegam habris, since Shabbos contains the whole Torah. He then relates the Eglei Tal's defense of the Shach, who allows a transgression to save a limb, against the kal vachomer from milah in Yoma: milah overrides Shabbos only because it too contains everything.

title.en: Why hilchos milah are in Maseches Shabbos

summary.en: The Rav shows that Shabbos and milah are both called bris and strengthen each other, and that all the laws of milah are taught through how milah falls on Shabbos. He asks why the perek opens with 'if he did not bring the tool' rather than with a new halacha, and answers that it continues the previous perek to show that hilchos milah are hilchos Shabbos.

title.en: Avraham's milah on Yom Kippur

summary.en: The Rav asks why Avraham, who kept the whole Torah, waited for his milah until commanded, and answers from Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer that he was circumcised on Yom Kippur, the Shabbos of Shabbosos and root of Shabbos. He adds that milah is called the greatest mitzvah and pegam habris the greatest aveirah, and both are tied to Yom Kippur.

title.en: The worth of learning in camp

summary.en: The Rav explains that every bit of Torah and every mitzvah of the smallest Jew raises the whole creation, and learning about milah is like fulfilling it. He urges the bachurim to use the precious time in camp with toil and chiddushim, and says that being sent to learn such Torah shows they are considered important in Heaven, like a president who sends only his best men on vital missions.

title.en: A great mission needs chizuk

summary.en: Like Moshe telling the meraglim to strengthen themselves, the Rav says a precious mission is a dangerous one: a truck of diamonds needs armor and two drivers. The yetzer hara will lie in wait with lashon hara, leitzanus and machlokes, and just as the Gemara has a soul sworn and strengthened before birth, one must ask Hashem for chizuk and take only the good.

title.en: Avodas hatefillah and the Ramban

summary.en: Turning to tefillah, the Rav says this generation must measure its davening against earlier ones and be ashamed of the weakness. Tefillah is avodah of the heart, and he brings the Ramban at the end of Parshas Bo: every mitzvah, even buying a mezuzah, rests on emunah, and the purpose of raising the voice in tefillah and of shuls is to proclaim publicly that we are Hashem's creations.

title.en: The Ba'al haTanya: daven together aloud

summary.en: The Rav brings the Ba'al haTanya, whose Shulchan Aruch is accepted everywhere, pleading that the tzibbur daven together word by word in a raised voice, not some loudly and others silently, as the Sefardim do. He adds that one asked by the gabbai to daven should not refuse, and that one with a fine voice must use it for Hashem, recalling Navos who withheld his voice.

title.en: The Pri Megadim and why we raise our voice

summary.en: The Rav goes through the poskim on a loud voice: the Beis Yosef on answering with all one's strength, the Kaf HaChaim citing the Eliyahu Rabbah, and the Pri Megadim, brought by the Mishnah Berurah, that one need not shout since Hashem hears. He answers that the voice is not for Hashem to hear but to arouse kavanah and wake the sleeping neshamah; only one who needs no such arousal may daven quietly.

title.en: Levels of hidden avodah; the Chafetz Chaim

summary.en: From the Shunamis, who needed signs to know Elisha was holy, the Rav explains that the higher a person stands, the less his avodah shows outside: yesharim sing and shout, tzaddikim less, chassidim and kedoshim hide it. He then brings the Chafetz Chaim, who writes that one should cry out to Hashem in tefillah, and the Stoliner Rebbe who davened aloud so chassidim would learn from him.

title.en: Every tefillah a Ne'ilah; closing charge

summary.en: The Rav asks the bachurim to test for themselves whether they daven better with warmth, and notes that even a cold shul shouts at Ne'ilah, though every tefillah is a diamond. With the Gemara on Iyov, punished for keeping silent, he explains that one who feels the pain cries out. He closes with Shabbos Parshas Korach, the sweetness of Hodu on Erev Shabbos, and a brachah to be good shluchim.

catalogTitle: חיזוק בתפילה: לעשות ריח ניחוח לה'' בא אתה וכל ביתך אל התיבה' רמב"ן פרשת בא' אגרות מבעל התניא ורבי ר' יונתן בעניני תפילה.

oneLiner.en: On Shiva Asar b'Tammuz, when the korban tamid ceased, the Rav calls for tefilah that is a 're'ach nichoach' to Hashem: davening with one's whole self, aloud, at length and together with the tzibbur, as the teivah that saves from the flood of the last generations.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with Shiva Asar b'Tammuz: the breaking of the luchos brought forgetfulness, so familiar things must be repeated, and since the tamid ceased, our tefillos stand in its place and must be a 're'ach nichoach'. He brings the Ba'al Shem Tov's reading of 'tzohar ta'aseh lateivah': a person must enter the teivah, the word of tefilah, with his whole self, for tefilah is Noach's ark against the flood of desires and heresy before Moshiach. He contrasts Torah and tefilah: learning wins honor while long davening is mocked, as the Gemara foresaw. From the Ramban at the end of Parshas Bo he shows that the purpose of creation is that people gather and proclaim before Hashem, and so tefilah needs a voice. He reads letters of the Ba'al HaTanya and Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz, tells stories about lateness and loud davening, describes the heichalos of pesukei dezimra, and closes with warnings against leitzanus and politics and a call to ahavas chaverim.

en: Since the tamid ceased, tefillah stands in its place, so a Jew's davening must itself be a 're'ach nichoach' that pleases Hashem.
Tefilah is Noach's teivah: the world is a flood of desires, and before Moshiach a flood of heresy, and one is saved by entering the words of davening with one's whole being.
Torah and tefilah need each other, yet people honor learning and mock long davening, which the Gemara calls a thing that stands at the height of the world and is treated lightly.
Following the Ramban, the purpose of creation and of the shul is that people gather to proclaim before Hashem that they are His creations, and so tefilah needs a voice.
Based on the Ba'al HaTanya's letters, the Rav teaches that davening should take its time, pesukei dezimra should be said together with the tzibbur, and the ba'al tefilah should not be rushed.
Each chapter and each word of davening is a heichal above, and one who says it together with the tzibbur enters the heichal with them.
In today's new trials the yeshiva is the place to flee to, and within it one must flee leitzanus and politics and hold on to ahavas chaverim.

candidateTopics: tefilah in place of the korban tamid
the teivah of tefilah and the flood

title.en: Forgetting, the tamid and a re'ach nichoach

summary.en: The Rav connects Shiva Asar b'Tammuz to the breaking of the luchos, which brought forgetfulness, and explains why things already heard must be repeated. Since the tamid ceased that day and tefillos stand in place of the tamid, he asks how our davening can be a 're'ach nichoach' for Hashem.

title.en: The teivah of tefilah against the flood

summary.en: After a self-deprecating mashal of a bus driver, the Rav brings the Ba'al Shem Tov on 'tzohar ta'aseh lateivah' and 'bo atah vechol beischa el hateivah': enter the word of tefilah with your whole self. Tefilah is the teivah that saves from the flood of desires and, before Moshiach, of heresy, and it is the defense against Amalek, who attacks the weak souls.

title.en: Torah and tefilah, and why davening is mocked

summary.en: The Rav contrasts Torah, the service of the mind, with tefilah, the service of the heart, and tells how the beis medrash was founded so that bochurim could keep davening as warmly as in camp. He insists Torah and tefilah need each other, then asks why learning brings honor while long davening is laughed at, and answers with the Gemara on things that stand at the height of the world.

title.en: The Ramban at the end of Parshas Bo

summary.en: The Rav reads the Ramban at the end of Parshas Bo: the purpose of creation is that man thank and acknowledge his Creator, and this is the purpose of shuls and of tefilah b'tzibbur, to gather and proclaim 'we are Your creations'. Through the Ramban he brings that tefilah needs a voice, 'chutzpah natzach l'bisha', overcoming the yetzer hara.

title.en: Why daven aloud

summary.en: The Rav answers those who mock loud davening: they themselves shout at Ne'ilah, and every tefilah should be a Ne'ilah. Only tzaddikim can daven quietly, as Rabbi Aharon of Karlin says; others must outshout the yetzer hara, which is itself loud, and he brings the Boyaner Rebbe's word that nowadays one must daven aloud with hislahavus.

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya's letters on davening

summary.en: The Rav reads the Ba'al HaTanya's letters: weekday davening should take about an hour and a half, businessmen must not rush the ba'al tefilah, and the long daveners should stand around him. He brings the Chasam Sofer's long davening as a bochur, the Gemara that one who lengthens his tefilah has his days lengthened, the teaching that in the time before Moshiach the main thing is tefilah, and the Ba'al HaTanya's plea that pesukei dezimra be said together, word by word.

title.en: Rabbi Aharon of Karlin and Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz

summary.en: The Rav tells how Rabbi Aharon of Karlin, called before a beis din for shouting in davening, answered that when a house burns one shouts. He then reads Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz's letter in Yaaros Devash: the young men laughed at his long Shemoneh Esrei, yet his portion from all his toil was the moments he stood before Hashem in tefilah.

title.en: Coming late: Bilgah and the late neshamah

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara at the end of Sukkah about the mishmar of Bilgah, whose ring was sealed because they came late, a sign the avodah was not dear to them, and compares it to a heart bypass. He then tells from Meir Einei HaGolah how a neshamah came to the Chidushei HaRim for a tikkun after the candles were lit, too late, because in its lifetime it came late to davening.

title.en: The heichalos of davening with the tzibbur

summary.en: The Rav explains why pesukei dezimra is said together: each chapter of Tehillim, and each word, is a heichal that opens only with the tzibbur. He goes through Shiras HaYam as a cheap segulah, Ahavah Rabbah, Emes Veyatziv and the descent of shefa after Shemoneh Esrei, with a mashal of paying for a watch and leaving without it, and then speaks of the ba'al tefilah who must lift the people and of learning as preparation for davening.

title.en: Fleeing into the yeshiva, and fleeing leitzanus

summary.en: The Rav describes the new temptations of today's inventions and the dangers of the street, and tells how the Satmar Rav, citing the Rambam that one should flee bad surroundings even to the desert, said that today one flees into the yeshiva. Inside the yeshiva too one must know whom to flee, above all a fixed habit of leitzanus, which uproots emunah.

title.en: Politics, ahavas chaverim and a closing tefilah

summary.en: The Rav warns against any involvement in politics and machlokes, then calls for ahavas chaverim, good friends who help and strengthen one another, as a foundation the Ba'al Shem Tov and the Arizal planted, and as a cure for the forces of Shiva Asar b'Tammuz. He closes with a tefilah for the rebuilding of Yerushalayim.

catalogTitle: The Significance of the 4 Methods of Destroying חמץ

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that the four ways of destroying chametz match the four elements, and that through them, as Avraham Avinu did with dust against the four kings, the Jews nullify the four kingdoms and the yetzer hara.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with a chaplain going to Jewish soldiers in Iraq and with Baghdad's place in Jewish history, from the yeshiva of Rav to the rivers of Bavel where the Levi'im wept. Turning to Rosh Chodesh Nisan, the Rosh Hashanah for kings, he explains that Nisan is a month of malchus and that Pesach is the Yom Tov of Avraham Avinu, whose victories, including the war against the four kings won with dust, came on Pesach. The four letters of Hashem's Name are the four elements; opposite them stand four klipos, the four kingdoms that captured Malchus Yisrael, which take many forms. Chametz is the yetzer hara, and the Mishnah's four ways of destroying it use wind, water, fire and, in bitul, earth. Ignoring the yetzer hara is Avraham's way. He links chametz and se'or to Edom and Yishmael, the four cups, and the twelve Nesi'im against Yishmael's twelve princes.

en: Nisan is the Rosh Hashanah for kings, a month of malchus, and Rosh Chodesh Nisan affects the whole year.
Pesach is the Yom Tov of Avraham Avinu and the midah of chesed, and his successes, including the victory over the four kings, all came on Pesach.
The four klipos opposite the four letters of Hashem's Name are the four kingdoms, which took the malchus of the Jewish people and must return it to Moshiach.
Chametz is the yetzer hara, and the four ways of destroying it in the Mishnah correspond to wind, water, fire and earth.
Bitul, declaring the chametz like the dust of the earth, is how Avraham Avinu defeated the four kings and how one should treat the yetzer hara: ignore it rather than argue with it.
Chametz, which is fit to eat, corresponds to Edom, from whom converts came; se'or, which is not, corresponds to Yishmael.
The twelve Nesi'im of Nisan stand against Yishmael's twelve princes, so the first twelve days of Nisan are a time to nullify Yishmael's power.

candidateTopics: Avraham Avinu and the war of the four kings
Nisan as the month of malchus

title.en: A chaplain going to Jewish soldiers in Iraq

summary.en: The Rav tells of a phone call from a former talmid, now an army chaplain, who was flying to Iraq with matzos for over a thousand Jewish soldiers. He says this gives a new dimension to the events there and that one must daven for these soldiers.

title.en: Baghdad, Bavel and the new Nebuchadnezzar

summary.en: The Rav describes Baghdad's Jewish past: Rav's yeshiva nearby, the cradle of the Talmud Bavli, and the graves of tzaddikim. He says the Iraqi ruler declared himself a new Nebuchadnezzar who would destroy Eretz Yisrael, and brings the promise that every weapon formed against the Jews will fail.

title.en: By the rivers of Bavel

summary.en: The Rav explains the kapitel of Tehillim about the rivers of Bavel, where the Levi'im refused to sing the song of Hashem for their captors and wept. He contrasts the outcry over Iraqi casualties at a checkpoint with Bavel's cruelty at the Churban, and reads the kapitel's ending as a decree that will be carried out by someone.

title.en: Rosh Chodesh Nisan, Rosh Hashanah for kings

summary.en: The Rav brings the Mishnah that the first of Nisan is the Rosh Hashanah for kings and explains that Nisan is a month of malchus. He tells of the Chozeh of Lublin's notebook for the year, ties Nisan to Yehuda and Nachshon ben Aminadav, reads 'Aviv' as father of twelve, and urges using the day for Torah, tefillah and bitachon.

title.en: Pesach, the Yom Tov of Avraham Avinu

summary.en: The Rav matches the three Yamim Tovim to the Avos and explains that Pesach belongs to Avraham Avinu and the midah of chesed, felt in the spring. He lists Avraham's events that came on Pesach, ending with his war against the four kings, whom he defeated by casting dust.

title.en: Four elements, four klipos, four kingdoms

summary.en: The Rav explains that the four letters of Hashem's Name are the source of the four elements, and opposite them are four klipos, the four kingdoms that captured the sparks of Malchus Yisrael and must return them to Moshiach. He brings the Maharal on why Yishmael is not counted, and the Ramban that Avraham's four kings correspond to the four kingdoms.

title.en: The klipos change form; chametz is the yetzer hara

summary.en: The Rav shows the four klipos in other forms: the four layers removed at a bris, the four marks of tzara'as, the four years of orlah, with the fourth, Edom, holding kedushah to be raised. He then brings the question of Tosafos why chametz is so stringent, and the Radbaz's conclusion from the Zohar that chametz is the yetzer hara.

title.en: The four ways of destroying chametz

summary.en: The Rav lays out the Mishnah's four ways of destroying chametz as wind, water, fire and, in bitul, earth, and explains that Avraham Avinu's dust was such bitul. He says one must not argue with the yetzer hara but ignore it, as Jews ignore the culture of the golus, and adds that the fourth klipah, Esav, holds good, since converts like Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Meir came from it.

title.en: The four cups, Mitzrayim and Yishmael

summary.en: The Rav brings the two sources for the four cups, the cups in Parshas Vayeshev and the four expressions of geulah, and explains that each cup has a good part and a bad part: at the makkos the wine poured out is a cup of poison for Mitzrayim, and the refilled cups are the cups of geulah. Yishmael, who began the golus by buying Yosef, is Mitzrayim's partner, and he reads Rabbi Yehuda's simanim as reaching Yishmael too.

title.en: Chametz and se'or: Edom and Yishmael

summary.en: The Rav explains that chametz, fit to eat, is Edom, and se'or, unfit, is Yishmael, so clearing out chametz is a war against them, as Avraham baking matzos defeated the four kings, hinted in the Midrash on Og. He says every scrub of the Pesach cleaning strikes the enemies of Yisrael, compares burning chametz to confusing the Satan with the shofar, and tells of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak watching women scrub their utensils.

title.en: Twelve Nesi'im against Yishmael; Hashem's malchus

summary.en: The Rav brings the Targum Yonasan that the twelve rams of the Nesi'im correspond to the twelve princes of Yishmael, who are to be lost, and urges using these twelve days with Torah, tefillah, tzedakah and helping prepare for Pesach. He closes with the Yismach Moshe's Rosh Hashanah drasha about Moshiach asking for his malchus, and with Nisan as the time of Hashem's malchus.

catalogTitle: סעודת הודאה: צריכים להודות לה' על כל נשימה ונשימה (צוואת יסוד ושורש העבודה)

oneLiner.en: At a seudas hodaah in Kislev, the Rav teaches that a Jew must thank Hashem for every breath and every small detail, drawing on the will of the author of Yesod V'Shoresh HaAvodah, and ends with the special thanks of a Jewish mother.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with Kislev as the month of hodaah, the Chanukah days set for Hallel and thanks. He explains Modim d'Rabbanan, where we thank Hashem for putting into our hearts the wish to thank Him, and the four people who must thank. From Dovid Hamelech's closing words, 'kol haneshamah', he learns that one must thank for every breath. He then reads from the will at the end of Yesod V'Shoresh HaAvodah, whose author thanked Hashem aloud for a private room, warm clothes, a snuffbox that did not spill and glasses that did not break, and calls this an exercise in emunah. The four who must thank are only examples for the wise man to learn from; two of the ten must be rabbanan, because the second finds what the first left out. He applies this to the seudah, to the beis medrash and to Kislev, and ends with the mother's mesirus nefesh, the hidden heart of the miracle, and Leah's thanks for a child.

en: Since everything that happens to a person comes from Hashem with hashgachah pratis, he must thank Him for every pleasure, large or small.
The verse 'kol haneshamah' teaches, as Chazal expound it, that one must thank Hashem for every single breath.
The will of Yesod V'Shoresh HaAvodah shows a Jew who thanked Hashem aloud, with joy, for each small kindness of his day.
The four who must thank are only headings; a wise man learns from them that there are hidden miracles every day, beginning with the workings of the body.
Hodaah is never finished, which is why two of the ten at a seudas hodaah must be rabbanan and why everyone adds his own Modim d'Rabbanan.
The hidden heart of the miracles of Yetzias Mitzrayim and Chanukah was the mesirus nefesh of righteous women, and a mother's thanks for a child is a thanks of its own kind.

title.en: Kislev, Modim and the four who must thank

summary.en: The Rav opens the seudas hodaah by calling Kislev the month of hodaah, explains Rashi on Modim d'Rabbanan that we thank Hashem for letting us thank, and asks why the Gemara gives the congregation its own text at Modim. He then brings the four who must thank and the rule that the thanks be said before ten, two of them rabbanan.

title.en: Thanks for every breath; the will of Yesod V'Shoresh HaAvodah

summary.en: From the end of Tehillim, 'kol haneshamah', the Rav learns that one must thank for every breath. He introduces the author of Yesod V'Shoresh HaAvodah, whose avodah the Chozeh of Lublin praised, and his will, written to teach his children rather than to boast.

title.en: Reading the will: thanks for each small kindness

summary.en: The Rav reads one item after another from the will: the author's thanks for a private room for avodah, for news of his children's health, for Shabbos clothes, a warm winter coat, answering Kedushah, having a needed item and the money for it, and for a fallen snuffbox, bottle and glasses that did not break. He calls this an exercise in emunah and adds that one must thank even when a shoelace does not tear.

title.en: The four are only examples: hidden daily miracles

summary.en: The Rav explains that the four who must thank are only headings: Hashem does great wonders 'alone', hidden ones no one sees. He describes the body's many systems, more delicate than a car of steel, and says that 'mi chacham' teaches a wise man to learn from the four to everything.

title.en: Why two rabbanan, and why Modim d'Rabbanan

summary.en: The Rav asks why two of the ten must be rabbanan and answers that the second chacham shows that after the first has finished there is still more to thank for, as Nishmas says. With this he answers his opening question: for hodaah the chazzan's words are not enough, so each one says Modim d'Rabbanan.

title.en: Korban todah, seudas hodaah and tonight's simcha

summary.en: Without a Beis Hamikdash, the seudas hodaah takes the place of the korban todah. The Rav brings the mefarshim on why the todah is eaten only for a day and a night: to bring more people and spread the thanks. He then names tonight's thanks for a child who came home well, to the doctors' wonder.

title.en: Thanks for the beis medrash and for every toothpick

summary.en: The Rav says the chaburah must thank Hashem for a beis medrash of serious ovdei Hashem with a warm, good davening, rare in today's cold times, and should use that gift. As Kislev comes, he urges taking on to thank for every detail, even a toothpick, as a fruit of emunah, hashgachah pratis and bitachon.

title.en: Thanking mothers: the hidden heart of the miracle

summary.en: The Rav praises the Oberland custom of thanking the mother after a meal and brings the Gemara that Leah was the first to thank Hashem. Through the Rashbam, that women were the main cause of the miracle, and Tosafos' question on him, he explains that the women's mesirus nefesh in Mitzrayim was the hidden heart of the redemption while Moshe and Aharon led openly.

title.en: Leah's thanks for a child; closing brachah

summary.en: The Rav explains that Leah, who already had three children, thanked for another as a mother building Klal Yisroel, a new kind of thanks; such is a mother's devotion at her child's hospital bed. He ties this to Chanukah, then blesses that all Jews thank Hashem together at the redemption, when even the galus will be understood as kindness.

catalogTitle: מטרת החסידות: לעבודת ה' ולאהבת חברים ולא להתחלק למפלגות.

oneLiner.en: The Rav teaches that the task of the generation before Moshiach is to serve Hashem with emes, and that true chassidus means love of friends and of every Jew rather than splitting into rival camps.

abstract.en: Speaking to a group of young men gathered to grow in fear of Heaven, the Rav notes that emes is the last word of Krias Shema, corresponding to the heel, the lowest generation before Moshiach. Emes is not written in the Torah's text; each generation must add it, and this generation's task is emes, though the Gemara says truth will then be missing. Truth is one, so when it becomes 'flocks and flocks', each group with its own truth, that is falsehood. The Ba'al Shem Tov built chassidus on emes, but its strength has faded. Reading from Shomer Emunim, the Rav explains that the essence of chassidus is love of the tzaddik, of friends and of all Jews; each group has its own root, but hating another group is the work of the Satan. Friends who share a root must care for one another, and even thinking badly of a friend, as a story of the Ba'al Shem Tov shows, gives power to the accuser.

en: Emes, the last word of Krias Shema, corresponds to the heel, the generation of ikvesa d'meshicha, whose task is to bring emes.
Truth is only one; when every group has its own 'truth', as in 'the truth will become flocks and flocks', it is not truth.
The work of today is to serve Hashem with emes, not for other motives.
The essence of chassidus is love of the tzaddik, of friends and of all Jews; division between chassidic groups is falsehood and the Satan's work.
Each group may have its own Rebbe according to its root, but one must love a fellow Jew even if he follows a different Rebbe.
Those who sit together share one root of soul and must care for one another first, while still loving every Jew.
Thinking badly of a fellow Jew is even worse than speaking badly, because thought reaches higher.

the derech of the Ba'al Shem Tov

title.en: Emes, the last word of Krias Shema

summary.en: The Rav opens with Yaakov Avinu and the attribute of emes. Each of the 248 words of Krias Shema corresponds to a limb, so the last word, emes, corresponds to the heel, which the Tanya compares to the lowest generation, ikvesa d'meshicha.

title.en: Our generation must add the emes

summary.en: The word emes is not in the Torah's parsha of Shema; we add it ourselves, because each generation has its task and the last generation's task is emes. He brings that before Moshiach truth will be missing, that emes is Hashem's seal, and that truth is only one, so 'flocks and flocks' of truths are not truth, illustrated with the time on a clock.

title.en: Chassidus built on emes, and its decline

summary.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov built chassidus on the attribute of emes, but falsehood will spread before Moshiach, so the work of young and old today is to serve Hashem with emes. Starting to read from Shomer Emunim, he describes the 150 years of the Ba'al Shem Tov's way, its great tzaddikim, and how it weakened, especially after the two world wars, leaving only an impression to hold on to.

title.en: The essence of chassidus: love of friends

summary.en: From Shomer Emunim the Rav reads that the essence of chassidus is love of the tzaddik, of friends and of all Israel, and that there must be peace between the chassidic groups. With the Chasam Sofer's twelve tribes and twelve gates, and the Sefardim and Ashkenazim following the Mechaber and the Rema, he explains that each root may have its own way and its own Rebbe.

title.en: Belonging to a team

summary.en: Bringing the Steipler, the Rav explains that every person wants to be great, and one who cannot becomes great through his team, like fans of ball teams. Chassidus today is often treated the same way; the Sanzer Rav rejected chassidim claiming their Rebbe is greater, and Shomer Emunim says hating a Jew because he is not of one's chassidim is not chassidus.

title.en: All hatred is falsehood

summary.en: Continuing Shomer Emunim, the Rav reads that one must love every Jew, especially those who keep mitzvos, and in this dark generation kiss the feet of every true believer. Every hatred is falsehood and the Satan's doing; the Ba'al Shem Tov, the greatest lover of Israel, never meant his way to divide Jews. This, the Rav says, is the truth that has become 'flocks and flocks'.

title.en: Those near in soul come first

summary.en: The Rav tells his listeners that they did not sit together by chance: they share one root of soul and stood near each other at Har Sinai. Like a relative who comes first for tzedakah, those close to one come first, yet every Jew must be loved. Serving Hashem with emes means loving Hashem, Jews and Torah; each Jew is a letter of the Sefer Torah and each group a parsha, all bound together.

title.en: Caring for a friend, and the snuff story

summary.en: The Rav describes love of friends in practice: caring about a friend's situation, davening and collecting money for him, joining his simcha and comforting him, and accepting the mitzvah of loving one's fellow before davening, as the Arizal says. He tells of a disciple of the Ba'al Shem Tov who was disturbed that a friend took snuff during davening, until he understood the friend needed it for strength, and was later told he had been an accuser.

title.en: Thought reaches higher than speech

summary.en: From the Chofetz Chaim the Rav explains that speaking against a Jew gives strength to the accuser above, and chassidic sefarim read 'do not join hands with the wicked' this way. Thinking badly is even worse, since thought reaches higher worlds than speech and deed; so one should think, speak and act well toward others, especially friends of one's root. He closes hoping to continue on love of friends another time.

catalogTitle: The Beginning of our Nuptials with Hashem

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains Pesach as the beginning and the opening of the bond between Hashem and Klal Yisrael, with the matzah as the key that opens a higher world for every Jew.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the idea that Pesach is the first stage of the nuptials between Hashem and Klal Yisrael, lesser than Shavuos and Sukkos, yet its prohibition of chametz carries kares, because eating matzah binds a Jew to Hashem just as strongly. Pesach is the reishis that holds everything, a time of renewal: the joy in Heaven in Nisan is mirrored in the reawakening of nature and in Shir Hashirim, and it is a time of techiyas hameisim and of becoming a new person. He then contrasts bread, which contains the ten utterances of creation and equals three times the Name of Hashem (78), with matzah, three times the full spelling of the Name (135), drawn from the world of 'Mah' that one can only ask about. Matzah is the key to rebirth and to opening up; Hashem knocks and asks Klal Yisrael to open for Him. He closes with tefillah for the geulah, seeing and being seen on Yom Tov, and wanting to be redeemed.

en: Pesach is the beginning of the bond between Hashem and Klal Yisrael, lesser than the later Yamim Tovim, yet its chametz prohibition carries kares because eating matzah binds a Jew to Hashem.
Pesach is the reishis that contains everything and a time of renewal, mirrored in the reawakening of nature in Nisan.
Bread contains the ten utterances of creation and therefore satisfies every kind of person, but its holiness is received only when one eats as a Jew should.
Matzah, equal to three times the full spelling of Hashem's Name, comes from a higher source than bread and is the key that opens a world beyond grasp.
On Pesach every Jew goes through a rebirth, and Hashem knocks on the door and asks Klal Yisrael to open up to Him.
Each Yom Tov has its gift; the gift of Pesach is geulah, and only one who wants it receives it.

candidateTopics: Pesach as the beginning of the bond with Hashem

title.en: Pesach as the first stage, and the kares of chametz

summary.en: The Rav describes Pesach as the beginning of the nuptials with Hashem, lesser than Shavuos and Sukkos (full Hallel, chametz still unfit), and asks why its prohibition alone carries kares. He answers that kares cuts the bond, while eating matzah creates hiskashrus, binding a Jew to Hashem.

title.en: Reishis, renewal and the joy of Nisan

summary.en: The Rav explains Pesach as the reishis that contains everything and as the renewal of the bond with Hashem. The joy in Heaven, shown in the tzeruf of Nisan from 'Yismechu hashamayim', comes down to earth: a new nation is born, nature wakes up in spring, and Shlomo HaMelech put this theme into Shir Hashirim.

title.en: Techiyas hameisim and becoming new

summary.en: The Rav brings the tradition that techiyas hameisim will be on Pesach and connects it to the dew of life, for which we begin praying on Pesach. He says it is a time for every Jew to make a reckoning and become a new person, and shows the flavor of newness in the custom of new clothes, dishes and painting for Pesach.

title.en: Bread holds the ten utterances

summary.en: The Rav explains why Hamotzi has ten words: bread contains the ten utterances of creation, just as man, created last, contains all traits, though each person has a dominant one. Therefore people need variety in food but never tire of bread; yet one who eats like Esav, without a bracha, receives klipah instead of that holiness.

title.en: The Malbim: how a Jew eats

summary.en: The Rav tells how the Malbim, after a debate with maskilim, said that they may know much, but he knows how to eat, and listed the many steps a Jew takes before he may eat. He adds that bread holds a threefold holiness, three times the Name of Hashem, equal to lechem (78), which gives life to the soul.

title.en: Matzah: three times Mah

summary.en: The Rav explains that matzah comes from a higher root than bread: Adam equals 45, the full spelling of the Name, called 'Mah', the world beyond grasp from which Yetzias Mitzrayim came. That is why the Seder opens with questions, and matzah, three times 45 (135), is the key to that world, eaten three times at the Seder.

title.en: The key of birth and opening

summary.en: The Rav explains Yetzias Mitzrayim as a birth, a nation taken from within a nation, and brings the Gemara that Hashem keeps the keys of birth and techiyas hameisim himself: on Pesach every Jew is reborn through the matzah. He connects this to 'peter rechem', to Targum's 'patira' for matzah, to the opening of the aron with Brich Shmei, and to 'Pischi li' in Shir Hashirim.

title.en: Tal, the matzah capsule and the open door

summary.en: The Rav explains that the tal (39, the first letters of the Name in full spelling) comes down to the final hei, Klal Yisrael, and that is the matzah. He brings the Ba'al HaTanya that the flour and water are only a capsule holding the same light as the matzah eaten in Mitzrayim, and ends with opening the door for Eliyahu HaNavi, since all of Pesach is an opening.

title.en: Tefillah for the King, re'iyah, and wanting geulah

summary.en: The Rav calls the day Rosh Hashanah for kings, when appointments are made in Heaven, and says one should daven that Hashem alone be King, with Moshiach as His chariot. He speaks of seeing Hashem and being seen on Yom Tov with completeness, and closes that the gift of Pesach is geulah, which only one who wants to be freed from the yetzer hara receives.

catalogTitle: Cell Phones: בענין קליפת "תכבד העבודה" בזמן הזה

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Pharaoh's decree 'let the work be made heavier' lives on today as a klipah of constant busyness, from phones and cell phones to social obligations and lavish simchas, that robs a Jew of any moment of calm reflection.

abstract.en: The Rav opens by saying he will repeat familiar things, as the Mesilas Yesharim says, because they need constant reminding. Following Reb Elchonon Wasserman, he presents the exile in Egypt as a model of today's exile: its last stretch was the hardest. When the Jews gathered on Shabbos to read scrolls promising redemption, Pharaoh decreed 'tichbad ha'avodah' so they would have no time to draw hope. Egypt was a 'house of slaves', a culture of work without thought. In Europe Jews were forced to toil, and a weary sigh at Minchah was precious; in America people choose the burden. Inventions save time, but the klipah fills it with new burdens: the telephone, then the cell phone, ringing in the beis medrash, and social pressures like kiddushes, nightly sheva brachos and costly weddings. He calls on each person to leave this Egypt and promises calm and joy from Heaven.

en: The Egyptian exile is a model of today's exile, and its final, hardest stage was Pharaoh's decree to make the work heavier.
Pharaoh's aim was to leave the Jews no time for the Shabbos gatherings where they drew hope from their scrolls of redemption.
Today too there is a klipah of 'tichbad ha'avodah': people are so busy and exhausted that they have no moment of yishuv hadaas to ask what they are doing in the world.
A Jew in Europe who was forced to toil was precious to Hashem, but one who chooses the burden in America is at fault.
Inventions save time, but the klipah fills the saved time with new burdens, above all the telephone and the cell phone.
Social pressures such as many kiddushes, nightly sheva brachos and lavish weddings are also part of this klipah, and one is not obligated to follow them.
Each person must decide to leave this Egypt, and one who frees himself is given calm and joy from Heaven.
