title.en: Sukkos as a return to Gan Eden

summary.en: The Rav calls Sukkos the strength of the whole year and explains that after Yom Kippur atones for Adam's sin, Jews are let back into the Garden of Eden, a place of joy. He introduces Hoshana Rabbah and Shemini Atzeres as the days of David and Shlomo, a likeness of the days of Moshiach.

title.en: Shemini Atzeres and Vezos Habracha

summary.en: The Rav explains that Shemini Atzeres is the peak of all the Yamim Tovim and is not called a chag, and that reaching it needs a teshuvah greater than Yom Kippur. He brings Reb Pinchas of Koretz on why Vezos Habracha is not counted among the Shabbos parshiyos, and explains that it belongs to a higher Shabbos.

title.en: The structure of parshas Re'eh

summary.en: The Rav surveys parshas Re'eh: it opens with eating before Hashem in Yerushalayim, turns to the meisis, the ir hanidachas and the forbidden animals, then returns to aser te'aser. He asks why the Torah does not join the beginning to the end, and begins to answer that eating is the gravest of acts, as the sin of the Eitz Hadaas shows.

title.en: Timtum halev and the four klipos

summary.en: The Rav explains that food becomes part of a person and forbidden food dulls the heart. He links Yechezkel's four klipos to the four exiles and the four impure animals, with the chazir as Edom, and contrasts the upright of heart who feel their bond with Hashem, which every Jew can reach in moments of dveikus.

title.en: Feeling the bond: the bas Levi and the Lechovitcher

summary.en: The Rav brings the Avnei Nezer on why a bas Levi who remarried on a single witness and was mistaken loses terumah: a wife feels her bond with her husband, and so the tribe of Levi felt its bond with Hashem. He tells how the Lechovitcher sensed his rebbe's passing, and reads Baal Peor and 've'atem hadveikim' the same way.

title.en: The meisis and forbidden food

summary.en: Returning to Re'eh, the Rav explains that holy eating binds a Jew to Hashem, and one who feels that bond cannot be swayed by a false prophet; the Torah then sets the forbidden animals right after the meisis. He brings the Toldos Yaakov Yosef's story from the Ba'al Shem Tov about the Rambam and those who questioned techiyas hameisim.

title.en: How did you fall? Lo sochal kol to'eivah

summary.en: The Rav reads the Torah after the meisis as crying out to the fallen Jew how he lost his dveikus, and answering: lo sochal kol to'eivah. He brings the Bnei Yissaschar in Igra DePirka from Reb Mendel of Rimanov on children who go off because of their parents' food, and the Bnei Yissaschar's conclusion that this is no excuse and one can purify himself.

title.en: Aser te'aser as the repair; the Shabbos meal

summary.en: The Rav explains the order of Re'eh: the opening speaks of an upright Jew, the middle of the damage of forbidden food, and the closing aser te'aser of the one who breaks through with teshuvah. He brings Reb Nachman's saying that one who believes he can damage must believe he can repair, and the Chiddushei HaRim that the Shabbos meal is a meal of emunah.

title.en: Holy places; the chazir as the last exile

summary.en: The Rav brings Reb Shalom of Belz that the air of the Beis Hamikdash is in the sukkah, and calls the beis medrash a holy place. He explains that the chazir is the worst of the four animals because it is Edom, the present exile, and brings the Midrash and a Shabbos zemer on the separate verse for it. He then brings the Gemara on the number of aliyos by the measure of bittul melacha.

title.en: Rosh Chodesh, women and the curse of melacha

summary.en: The Rav brings Rashi and Tosafos that women refrain from work on Rosh Chodesh because they did not give their jewelry to the egel, and the Tzlach's question why there are four aliyos when the men work. He explains that melacha is a curse that came from Adam's eating, that days of brachah such as Shabbos and Yom Tov are free of it, and that the women's brachah on Rosh Chodesh spreads to their husbands.

title.en: Days of brachah; why women merited Rosh Chodesh

summary.en: The Rav shows that kohanim, Yerushalayim, shemitah and a chassan and kallah are bound up with brachah and kept from melacha. He brings Reb Tzadok that Rosh Chodesh will be holier than Shabbos in the future, and the Baal HaTanya on matzah as daas and wine as feeling, and concludes that women, who felt the bond at the egel, merited Rosh Chodesh, which needs that feeling; he adds David and Shaul's seudah.

title.en: The repair: holy eating at home

summary.en: The Rav says that even those who ate forbidden food in times of persecution on a rav's ruling still carry timtum halev, and its repair is holy eating in a holy place. He explains that after Shemini Atzeres the sukkah goes into the home, and describes the Shabbos table, netilas yadayim and bentching with kavanah from a siddur, bringing the Mishnah Berurah, the Rokeach and the Sefer HaChinuch.

title.en: Shemini Atzeres: love, teshuvah and protection

summary.en: The Rav calls Shemini Atzeres a day of pure love when the heart opens to Hashem, brings Reb Shalom of Belz and the Minchas Elazar on davening with kavanah on these three days, and explains that this teshuvah with the whole heart is why aser te'aser is read then. He closes with the sukkah as protection for all Jews and the world, and a brachah.

catalogTitle: מוצאי שמיטה: במוצאי שביעית בן דוד בא; כי שנה השמינית הוא בחינת לעתיד לבא

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that after the seven of shemitah comes the 'eighth', a glimpse of yovel and the world of Moshiach, which is why the Gemara says Moshiach comes at the end of shemitah and why the Rosh Hashanah and Hakhel after shemitah carry a special hope.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the mitzvah of appointing a king, asking why asking Shmuel for a king was resented. Turning to the Elul after shemitah and the coming Hakhel, he reviews that Yerushalayim is a permanent shemitah, and that shemitah is its overflow over all of Eretz Yisrael, so shemitah is entirely tosefes; this explains why the law of tosefes is learned from shemitah, and by Rabbi Akiva. Yovel, Shavuos and Yom Kippur are the 'eighth', above the seven days of nature, as the Maharal writes about Chanukah and milah. The Kodesh HaKodashim is where heaven meets earth, so the aron took no space. The end of Shabbos and of shemitah touches the eighth, hence melave malka, Moshiach coming after shemitah, and Hakhel. Children are brought to Hakhel in hope of singing shirah, and no waiting for Moshiach is wasted. He closes urging all to accept Hashem as King.

en: Yerushalayim is a constant shemitah; in the seventh year its 'spring' overflows over all of Eretz Yisrael and every Jew becomes like a kohen.
All of shemitah is tosefes on Yerushalayim, which is why the halachah of tosefes is learned from shemitah rather than from Shabbos or Yom Kippur.
The 'eighth' level, yovel, Shavuos, Yom Kippur and the Kodesh HaKodashim, stands above the seven days of creation and belongs to the days of Moshiach.
At the end of every Shabbos and every shemitah the eighth draws near, which is why Moshiach is expected after shemitah and why melave malka is David's meal.
Hakhel in the eighth year joins the king, the heart of the nation, with Yerushalayim, the heart of place, and is a time when the eighth world may be revealed.
No Jew's waiting for Moshiach is wasted; every hope joins the waiting of all generations and brings Moshiach closer.

title.en: Why asking Shmuel for a king was resented

summary.en: The Rav reads the parsha of appointing a king and the Rambam that it is a mitzvah, and asks why the request to Shmuel was resented. He notes from the Gemara about Shaul that Shmuel already functioned as king, and asks why they did not simply appoint him.

title.en: Elul after shemitah and the coming Hakhel

summary.en: The Rav notes that it is Elul at the end of shemitah, with Hakhel due on Sukkos. He brings the Chasam Sofer that after a year of Torah the Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Sukkos are greater, and says that to understand Hakhel one must understand shemitah and yovel.

title.en: Yerushalayim as a constant shemitah

summary.en: Reviewing an earlier year's shiur, the Rav explains that Yerushalayim is always in a state of shemitah: Torah study, hefker, no planting, no tribal ownership, the city of kohanim. In the seventh year this overflows over all of Eretz Yisrael and every Jew becomes like a kohen.

title.en: Tosefes is learned from shemitah

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara that Rabbi Akiva learns tosefes from the extra verse about plowing and harvest, said of shemitah, and asks why it is not learned from Yom Kippur. He answers that shemitah itself is tosefes on Yerushalayim, and explains why it is specifically Rabbi Akiva, a ben ger, who teaches it.

title.en: Yovel and the eighth level, with the Maharal

summary.en: The Rav explains that yovel is the Kodesh HaKodashim: the Torah was heard on the fiftieth day and the luchos came down on Yom Kippur, both glimpses of yovel. He brings the eight-stringed harp of Moshiach and reads the Maharal that the Kodesh HaKodashim, Chanukah, milah and the Torah are 'after seven', the eighth above nature.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai as yovel

summary.en: The Rav explains the dispute between Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai about working the land: Rashbi is the aspect of Shabbos, and even more, of yovel, the 'Shabbos of Shabbosos'. From the Gemara that 'hod' is the Beis HaMikdash he calls Rashbi the hod within hod, the Kodesh HaKodashim, and says Shavuos and Yom Kippur are both glimpses of yovel.

title.en: The aron that took no space

summary.en: The Rav asks why the aron taking no space is not counted among the miracles of the Beis HaMikdash, and what purpose it served. He answers that the Kodesh HaKodashim, where creation began, is where heaven meets earth, and heaven is above measure, so it is its nature, not a miracle; likewise Rabbi Yehuda's fiftieth year counts for both cycles, and Moshe could add a day.

title.en: Why the children come to Hakhel

summary.en: The Rav brings the derashah of Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah on Hakhel: the men come to learn, the women to hear, and the children to give reward to those who bring them. He asks why Hashem would give a mitzvah whose only point is reward, with no purpose of its own.

title.en: David's fourth tefillah and fourth seudah

summary.en: The Rav discusses David's prayer at chatzos and the Ramchal that it is not obligatory because David was lower than the Avos, and questions this from Midrash Tanchuma and the Gemara that Moshiach is greater than the Avos. He compares the three Shabbos meals to the Avos and melave malka to David, and explains why the end of Shabbos, bordering on the eighth, is its holiest moment.

title.en: Moshiach comes after shemitah

summary.en: The Rav explains the Gemara that Moshiach comes at the end of shemitah: after seven comes eight, the world of Moshiach. He describes Moshiach's soul waiting in heaven, the tzaddik of each generation fit to receive it, and the doubt in heaven at every end of Shabbos and shemitah whether the next is the eighth or a new first, which also deepens Rabbi Yehuda's view of the fiftieth year.

title.en: Magen David and maftir

summary.en: The Rav brings the Zohar that David asked for a blessing like 'Magen Avraham' and was tested with Bas Sheva. He asks why 'Magen David' is said in the haftarah blessings but not in Shemoneh Esrei, and answers that David's greatness will only be understood in the eighth world of Moshiach, which maftir, the eighth aliyah, represents.

title.en: Rosh Hashanah and Hakhel in the eighth year

summary.en: The Rav explains why the eighth year is still called 'the year of shemitah' and says the coming Rosh Hashanah is the 'shalosh seudos' of shemitah, tosefes upon tosefes. He reads the Rambam on Hakhel as a renewed Sinai and on the king as the heart of Israel, and explains that the king, Yerushalayim and Yom Kippur are the heart in soul, place and time, joining at Hakhel in the eighth year.

title.en: No waiting for Moshiach is wasted

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara against those who calculate the end, and its answer that one waits in order to receive reward, 'fortunate are all who wait for Him'. He explains that every Jew's hope joins the waiting of all generations and brings Moshiach closer, like money accumulating in an account.

title.en: The children's shirah and the hope of Hakhel

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara that infants sang shirah at the Yam Suf and pointed, and says the future song will be greater. This answers his question: at Hakhel after shemitah the eighth world might be revealed, so parents bring their children in hope they will sing. When it did not come in hundreds of Hakhels, he answers as the Gemara does: the waiting is never wasted.

title.en: Accepting Hashem as King this Rosh Hashanah

summary.en: Returning to the mitzvah of appointing a king, the Rav says the Rosh Hashanah after shemitah is an auspicious time for Moshiach, and one must prepare to accept Hashem as King instead of the desires that rule a person's life. He describes Moshiach's soul hovering like a bird looking for rest, leaves the opening questions unanswered for lack of time, and closes with blessings for a good year.

catalogTitle: דרשה בבית האסורים: English: Freedom in Prison אידיש: גודל תענוג השכינה מעבודה בעמקי הקליפות

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that the light Hashem created on the first day is true freedom from the yetzer hara, and that accepting the kingship of Heaven even from the lowest place, as Yosef did when he left prison on Rosh Hashana, is what makes a person free.

abstract.en: The Rav opens in English on the twenty-fifth of Elul, the first day of creation, when Hashem said 'Let there be light'. He explains that light means happiness, contentment and above all liberty, and that real liberty is being free to do the right thing; the greatest imprisonment is being bound to the yetzer hara, and the whole world is in that sense a big prison. Every person has an inner desire to serve his Creator, and the world awaits a Rosh Hashana when all mankind will hear Hashem's voice and be free to serve Him. After blessing his listeners, he continues in Yiddish with Tanya chapter 33: the purpose of creation is to bring holiness down to the lowest places, and serving Hashem from darkness, in galus and outside Eretz Yisrael, brings Him special joy. He ties this to Rosh Hashana as the day of malchus, to the chazan saying 'Hamelech' where he stands, and to Yosef leaving prison on Rosh Hashana, and closes with the shofar of freedom.

en: The light Hashem created with 'Let there be light' means happiness, contentment and above all liberty.
Real liberty is being free to do the right thing, and the greatest imprisonment is being bound by the yetzer hara and one's bad passions.
Every human being has an inner desire to serve Hashem, his Creator and Provider, and the world awaits a Rosh Hashana when all mankind will be free to serve Him.
Following Tanya chapter 33, the Rav teaches that the main purpose of creation is to bring holiness down to the lowest places, and that this should give a Jew great joy wherever he finds himself.
Rosh Hashana is the time of accepting the kingship of Heaven, and malchus is brought down to the lowest place where a Jew stands.
A Jew in the lowest state, even in prison, must know that he has a mission from Hashem there and accept the kingship of Heaven there; whoever does so is a king and is free.

candidateTopics: Rosh Hashana and kingship of Heaven
avodah in galus and chutz la'aretz

title.en: Let there be light: light is liberty

summary.en: Speaking in English, the Rav explains that the twenty-fifth of Elul is the day of creation and that Rosh Hashana falls on the sixth day, when Adam was created. He interprets the light of 'Let there be light' as happiness and liberty, and describes the greatest prison as being bound by the yetzer hara.

title.en: Awaiting a Rosh Hashana of freedom

summary.en: The Rav says that on the first day Hashem meant freedom to serve Him, which every person inwardly desires, and that the world awaits a Rosh Hashana when all mankind will hear Hashem's voice and be free. He blesses his listeners with a kesivah vachasimah tovah and announces that he will continue in Yiddish.

title.en: Tanya 33: serving Hashem from the depths

summary.en: The Rav brings Tanya chapter 33, that the purpose of creation is to bring holiness into the lowest places and that subduing the sitra achra there brings Hashem joy. He applies this to serving Hashem in chutz la'aretz and in the last generations of galus, and to the Rosh Hashana theme of malchus and the cry 'from the depths'.

title.en: Yosef leaves prison on Rosh Hashana

summary.en: The Rav suggests that this is why there is no aliyah l'regel on Rosh Hashana and why the chazan says 'Hamelech' where he stands. He explains that on Rosh Hashana Yosef left prison, the place of greatest lowliness, and that whoever accepts the kingship of Heaven there is a king and free; he closes with the shofar of freedom and blessings.

catalogTitle: Why the תלמידי ר' עקיבא Stopped Dying When the Week of ל”ג בעומר Arrived

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Rabbi Akiva's talmidim died because they honored each other only for visible virtues, and that the dying stopped in the week of Hod when Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, revealer of the Torah's secrets, taught them that every Jew carries a hidden secret that makes him precious to Hashem.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with a saying that whoever believes in Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai can draw chizuk from him, since he is for every Jew. He asks how Rabbi Akiva's talmidim could have failed to respect each other. Just as the Torah has pshat, remez, drush and sod, every Jew has a hidden sod; citing the Chiddushei HaRim, he says every Jew finds unique favor with Hashem through a trait no one can identify. The talmidim respected only visible greatness, so the respect between chavrusos ran one way. The week of Hod, the middah of yielding, calls for honoring even a lesser chavrusa. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who revealed the Torah's secrets after the Churban, taught this on Lag BaOmer, his day, and the decree ended. Pesach Sheini, given to the temei'im in the week of Hod, and the link between Lag BaOmer and Purim show the same point, as does the Ohr HaChaim's teaching that the final day of redemption comes even for complete reshaim.

en: Just as the Torah has pshat, remez, drush and sod, every Jew has a hidden sod that no one else can see.
The sin of Rabbi Akiva's talmidim was that respect between chavrusos went only from the lesser to the greater, based on visible virtues.
Hod is the middah of yielding and subordination, and its tikkun is to respect even a chavrusa who is lesser in every visible way.
Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who revealed the secrets of the Torah, taught the talmidim on Lag BaOmer that every Jew carries a sod, and then the decree ended.
Pesach Sheini, a special day given to the temei'im in the week of Hod, shows that every Jew has a sod for which he is worthy.
Lag BaOmer and Purim share one character: both show that Hashem finds favor even in the lowest Jew.
The final day of the Geulah, which comes even for complete reshaim, is itself a sod, because it comes through the sod in every Jew.

candidateTopics: the hidden secret in every Jew
Sefirah and the middah of Hod
the final date of the Geulah

title.en: Chizuk from Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and the question

summary.en: The Rav opens with a saying that whoever believes in Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai can draw chizuk from him, as he is for every Jew, like Hashem. He raises the question of how Rabbi Akiva's talmidim could have failed to respect each other, and introduces pshat, remez, drush and sod, with sod revealed by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, paralleled by the four levels of the soul.

title.en: Every Jew is a letter in the Sefer Torah

summary.en: The Rav explains that the 600,000 souls correspond to the letters of the Torah: each is unique, and a missing letter invalidates the Sefer Torah. He brings the Chiddushei HaRim that every Jew finds special favor with Hashem through a trait of his own, and that no one can know in this world which trait it is.

title.en: The hidden sod and the one-way respect

summary.en: The Rav explains that every Jew has pshat, remez, drush and a hidden sod known only to Hashem. Rabbi Akiva's talmidim judged each other by visible virtues: among the 12,000 pairs of chavrusos, the lesser respected the greater but not the reverse, and that was their flaw.

title.en: The week of Hod: the middah of yielding

summary.en: The Rav goes through the seven middos of the weeks of Sefirah and explains Netzach and Hod as the two legs that support the body: victory and yielding. Hod is surrender, as in the reed that bends before the wind, and its tikkun is to respect even a lesser chavrusa because he has something one lacks.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai reveals the secrets

summary.en: The Rav asks who made the talmidim aware of the hidden sod in every Jew, and answers: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, then a youngster among them. Like Yechezkel, who saw the Merkavah after the first Churban to encourage the Jews in galus, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai revealed the Zohar after the second Churban.

title.en: Lag BaOmer: his day, and the decree ends

summary.en: The Rav explains that every person has a day when his mazal is strongest, and Lag BaOmer is Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's day. On that day he succeeded in teaching the talmidim to respect even a lesser chavrusa because of the sod he carries, the talmidim began respecting each other and the decree ended, and so it is a double simcha.

title.en: Pesach Sheini: a day for the temei'im

summary.en: The Rav asks what the temei'im who said 'lamah nigara' were arguing, since their impurity obviously excluded them, and why Moshe did not answer them directly. He explains that Pesach celebrates becoming Jews, so Hashem agreed and gave them the first day of Hod; why that date was chosen has no answer, since it is a sod, like the hidden worth of every Jew.

title.en: Lag BaOmer and Purim

summary.en: The Rav connects Lag BaOmer to Purim, the Yom Tov for the low and the stragglers whom Amalek attacked. He brings the Shulchan Aruch's at-bash rule, in which 'peleg' teaches that Lag BaOmer falls on the same weekday as Purim, and concludes that Hashem even made a special Yom Tov, Pesach Sheini, for the impure.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon for every Jew, and the sod of the Geulah

summary.en: The Rav returns to the opening saying: emunah in Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is emunah in the sod of the Torah, which tells even the simplest Jew that he is precious to Hashem. He brings the Ohr HaChaim, similar to the Ramban, that the final day of the Geulah comes even for complete reshaim because of the sod in every Jew, and closes that there are secrets in the Torah, in every Jew and in the Geulah.

catalogTitle: גודל כח סעודת מרעים: מקבלים השפעות גדולות מציל ממים הזידונים של גלות

oneLiner.en: At a melave malka held as a farewell seudah for a friend, the Rav explains that Jews who eat together are bound into one group that receives a higher flow of life, and that this bond is a teivah that saves them from the waters of the present exile.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with melave malka as a seudah that escorts Shabbos and traces the farewell seudah to Shemini Atzeres. He tells a story from the Midrash, cited in teshuvos of the Divrei Chaim and the Chiddushei HaRim, of a couple who parted with a seudah and were then blessed with children. He then explains that Hashem sends greater hashpa'ah to a tzibbur, which becomes a new collective soul, and that eating together forms a zimun the same way; 'yachdav' means bound, not merely together. The Midrash reads the four 'vayigberu' of the Mabul as the four exiles, and the present Mabul of heresy is escaped through the teivah: Torah, tefillah and joining with friends. Finally he links the thirty letters of a line in a Sefer Torah to the chaburos of the korban Pesach, and applies all this to the seudah for their friend Menachem.

en: A tzibbur of ten becomes a new entity with a collective soul and can receive a hashpa'ah that even the greatest individual tzaddik cannot.
Eating is a receiving of life, and when several Jews eat together they form a zimun that receives a higher kind of life; the bond of zimun comes from the eating, not from the benching.
The Midrash teaches that the four times 'vayigberu' appears by the Mabul are the four exiles, so the Mabul is a living lesson for galus.
The way to be saved from today's Mabul is to run into the teivah: Torah, tefillah, Tehillim, and binding oneself with friends.
A line of thirty letters in a Sefer Torah corresponds to the three groups of ten in which the korban Pesach was slaughtered and eaten.

candidateTopics: the Mabul as an image of galus
the teivah as words of Torah and tefillah
friendship among those who fear Hashem

title.en: Melave malka and the farewell seudah

summary.en: The Rav describes melave malka as a small seudah escorting Shabbos as it leaves and traces the farewell seudah to Shemini Atzeres. He begins a teshuvah of the Divrei Chaim about a talmid chacham married ten years without children.

title.en: The couple who parted with a seudah

summary.en: The Rav relates that the same question was sent to the Chiddushei HaRim, who ended with the Midrash of the childless couple who came to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai to divorce, parted with a seudah, and were blessed with children through his tefillah. He adds what a Sanzer descendant told him about the family's tradition.

title.en: Hashpa'ah to a tzibbur and through eating

summary.en: The Rav explains that Hashem sends each soul hashpa'ah through Torah, tefillah and eating, measured to what it can hold, and that ten Jews joined as a tzibbur become a new entity that receives more. Eating as a Jew should eat draws a holier kind of life, and several eating together form a zimun, which already brings the Shechinah with three.

title.en: Zimun comes from eating; 'yachdav' means bound

summary.en: The Rav brings the Chiddushei HaRim's reason why chassidim eat together after davening, and shows that the bond of zimun comes from eating together, not from benching together. From the passuk of zimun and the laws of shaatnez he proves that 'yachdav' means bound, not merely side by side.

title.en: Eating creates friendship; Ammon and Moav

summary.en: The Rav says eating together creates lasting friendship and connection. Using the principle that not believing in techiyas hameisim is a sign rather than a punishment, he explains that Ammon and Moav's failure to bring bread and water showed they have no connection to the Jewish people.

title.en: The Mabul of today and the teivah

summary.en: The Rav brings the Midrash that the four times 'vayigberu' are the four exiles, so the Mabul repeats itself in galus, and today's Mabul is one of heresy and immorality. Citing the Ba'al Shem Tov that a teivah is a word of Torah and tefillah, he says a Jew must flee into it, as Noach did, and those who bind themselves to the tzaddikim will remain.

title.en: The four exiles: breadth, height and time

summary.en: The Rav describes each exile: Bavel scattered the Jews in breadth, Madai brought Haman's decree, Yavan fought in height against the Shechinah, matching the fifteen amos the waters rose, and Edom contains them all and adds the dimension of time, an exile without a set end, matching the hundred and fifty days. The answer remains to flee into the teivah of Torah and tefillah.

title.en: Joining with friends as a teivah

summary.en: The Rav says binding with friends is part of the teivah, bringing the Ruzhiner Rebbe's advice that Jews should gather and strengthen each other, and the command to Noach to take food into the teivah. He cites Malachi that in the final hester panim those who fear Hashem speak to one another, and tells of a talmid who complained that people come to sit with him, and was told that this itself is a great strength.

title.en: Thirty letters in a line and the korban Pesach

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara that a line in a Sefer Torah holds thirty letters, 'lemishpechoseichem' three times, and asks why it is learned from the korban Pesach and not from the earlier 'lemishpechoseihem' by Noach. He explains that souls come down in groups, that the korban Pesach was eaten in chaburos and slaughtered in three groups of thirty, and that leaving the teivah broke the group while the Pesach gathered it.

title.en: This seudah and the parting from Menachem

summary.en: The Rav applies the ideas to the gathering: they are eating a melave malka bound to Shabbos and parting from their friend Menachem, and eating together binds them. He contrasts a passuk, which cannot be split, with a flexible line, and closes that everything written about the Mabul is a lesson for galus, noting the first passuk of Zichronos about Noach.

catalogTitle: Cell Phones: כינוס התעוררות בענין: חומר סכנת Cell Phones בלי הכשר

oneLiner.en: The Rav warns the young men of his shul against cellphones without a hechsher, from the leitzanus of text messages to the danger of immorality, and insists that the ruling of the Gedolim must be obeyed.

abstract.en: Speaking in the days of Selichos to the young men raised in his shul, the Rav addresses a report that some have become absorbed in their cellphones. Text messages, he explains, remove the natural shame of face-to-face speech and breed a constant traffic of jokes and leitzanus, even during learning and davening. He brings a story of someone who left a meal rather than sit in a moshav leitzim, and the passuk that one cannot sit among scoffers and desire Hashem's Torah at once. New tools are new forms of the yetzer hara. Far worse, a phone with open features exposes a person to immorality. Using the Gemara in Bava Basra and the Rashbam, he explains that only someone who truly needs it for his livelihood may use one, and compares this to a heter given only for a pressing case. Ignoring the Gedolim's ban, he argues from zaken mamrei, Rabbeinu Yonah and the fall of American Jewry, cuts a person off from Hashem. He ends with practical guidance and a call to tefillah.

en: Text messages remove the shame of speaking face to face, so they become a channel for constant jokes and leitzanus.
A person cannot both sit among scoffers and truly desire Hashem's Torah; it is one or the other.
A cellphone with open features exposes its owner to the danger of immorality, which is far graver than leitzanus.
Only someone who must have such a phone for his livelihood may use it, and then he must guard himself; one who does not need it and takes it anyway is called a rasha.
Disobeying the Gedolei Yisrael who forbade such phones is akin to the sin of the zaken mamrei and cuts a person off from Hashem.
The Rav calls on those without a business need to decide now to get rid of such a phone, and on everyone to daven daily for protection from the yetzer hara.

candidateTopics: new forms of the yetzer hara
Shlomo HaMelech and the king's wives

title.en: Text messages and the loss of shame

summary.en: The Rav addresses the young men raised in his shul, says it is a time of seeking Hashem, and relates the report that some are absorbed all day in their cellphones. He explains that text messages remove the shame of face-to-face speech, breed leitzanus, and distract bochurim even during the shiur and davening.

title.en: Leaving a moshav leitzim

summary.en: The Rav tells of a man who got up and left a family meal when a joke was made, because it was a moshav leitzim, and contrasts this with devoting a whole day to leitzanus by text. He tells the young men they are too choshuv to fall to such lowness.

title.en: Learning is Shabbos; new yetzer haras

summary.en: The Rav says that during learning one treats the phone as on Shabbos, and that even a kosher phone does not belong in the beis medrash. One cannot both sit among scoffers and desire Hashem's Torah. He then speaks of new forms of the yetzer hara, such as movies and radio, that keep appearing.

title.en: A trembling world and the Mississippi drasha

summary.en: The Rav describes a time when the world is in turmoil and dangers loom, and tells how the Chofetz Chaim gathered people for a drasha on teshuvah because the Mississippi had flooded in America. When Hashem shakes the world, he says, the message is for Jews; mocking such things by text is laughable, and the phone holds something worse than leitzanus.

title.en: The danger of zenus and the one who closes his eyes

summary.en: The Rav warns that a phone with open features exposes a person to immorality, citing the passuk not to approach the door of her house. Rabbanim allowed it only for business; he brings the Gemara in Bava Basra and the Rashbam that one who walks a road of temptation without need is a rasha even if he shuts his eyes, while one with no other way becomes a ba'al bechirah who must guard himself.

title.en: A heter for one is treif for another

summary.en: The Gedolim forbade such phones and permitted them only for business. Through a mashal of two shailos on meat, one before Shabbos when the Rav relies on the Rema's leniency for a pressing case and one on Sunday, the Rav shows that what is permitted for one is forbidden for another. He adds that a single look can harm a person for life, and that zenus belongs to the sins of yehareg ve'al ya'avor.

title.en: Zaken mamrei and the yud of yarbeh

summary.en: The Rav says disobeying the rabbanim is worse still: the Rambam calls the parsha of zaken mamrei the foundation of the Torah. He tells of Shlomo HaMelech, who relied on his own wisdom to take more wives, and asks why it was the yud of 'yarbeh' that complained; the yud stands for bitul, as Moshe added a yud to Yehoshua's name for his humility.

title.en: The Gedolim's ruling and Rabbeinu Yonah

summary.en: The Rav stresses that the Gedolim of America and Eretz Yisroel forbade phones without a hechsher except for a business need, and one who disobeys is like a zaken mamrei. He brings the Gemara in Berachos and Rabbeinu Yonah, who explains the death penalty for disregarding the rabbanim, and the passuk of the judge 'in those days'; cleaving to talmidei chachamim is how one cleaves to Hashem.

title.en: Decide now; why American Jewry fell

summary.en: The Rav says the gadol hador has the status of one's main rebbe, and calls on whoever has such a phone without a business need to decide now to give it up despite the cost. He explains that American Jews fell away because they did not listen to the rabbanim about kashrus, and that the word 'zadon' marks undermining the foundation of Yiddishkeit.

title.en: Who may use it, and how

summary.en: The Rav praises the young men and says one must daven daily to be saved from the yetzer hara. He gives the example of a mechanech who must reach doctors and psychologists for his students: such a person may use it, but only during business hours, like chametz that is kosher all year and becomes treif. Doubts should go to a moreh hora'ah, and the principle of 'once permitted for a need' does not apply here.

title.en: No half-measures; tefillah and a brachah

summary.en: Blocking text service by calling the company is no real solution, since it can be restored with one call; the only solution is not to have it, and the main one is to ask Hashem for help. The tests of this generation come because it is being prepared for Moshiach, and the talk ends with blessings for the new year.

catalogTitle: The מדה of הוד and its Connection to רשב”י

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains why Lag BaOmer, hod shebehod and the day of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, belongs to every Jew: Rashbi, the Kohen Gadol of the hidden Torah, revealed that every Jew carries a hidden point in which he is irreplaceable.

abstract.en: The Rav sets out to explain the Bnei Yissaschar's words that, just as Hashem is for everyone, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and Lag BaOmer are for everyone, even the lowest. Hod, the fifth middah, means yielding and is the Beis HaMikdash; Lag BaOmer, hod shebehod, is the Kodesh HaKodashim, a place above time, space and nature, and Rashbi, who revealed the hidden Torah, is the Kohen Gadol after the churban, whom mourning does not touch. The students of Rabbi Akiva did not honor one another because they did not see that every Jew, like every letter in the Sefer Torah, has a hidden point in which he is irreplaceable. The Rav connects this to combining sedras in seasons of achdus, to stories of the Satmar Rav and the Arizal in Meron, to Purim, which is also hod, and to the 33rd letter of Baruch Shem and Shema.

en: Hod is the middah of yielding and is the Beis HaMikdash; its place is the Beis HaMikdash, its soul is Aharon and the kohanim, and its time is the week of Lag BaOmer.
Lag BaOmer, hod shebehod, is the Kodesh HaKodashim, above time, space and nature, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is the Kohen Gadol who enters it after the churban.
Every Jew corresponds to one of the 600,000 letters of the Sefer Torah and has a point in which he is irreplaceable and surpasses even the greatest tzaddik.
The students of Rabbi Akiva failed to honor one another because they did not see the hidden superiority of each friend; Rashbi revealed that every Jew has such a side.
In seasons tied to redemption a breach of achdus is graver, and so sedras are combined then, against the usual rule not to mix them.
Purim, like Lag BaOmer, is hod: both fall on the same day of the week, both are a mystery, and on both even the lowest Jew rejoices.

candidateTopics: Kodesh HaKodashim and the Kohen Gadol
every Jew as a letter in the Sefer Torah

title.en: Hod: the Beis HaMikdash and Aharon

summary.en: The Rav reads the Bnei Yissaschar that Lag BaOmer, like Hashem, is for everyone, even the lowest, and sets out to explain it. He brings the Gemara in Berachos that hod is the Beis HaMikdash, ties Lag BaOmer in parshas Emor to the kohanim and to Aharon, the fifth of the seven shepherds, and defines hod as yielding, like grass that bends in a storm.

title.en: The Kohen Gadol and the Kodesh HaKodashim

summary.en: The Rav explains that the Sefirah mourning for Rabbi Akiva's students ends on Lag BaOmer because hod is the Beis HaMikdash, which mourning does not reach, as the Torah says the Kohen Gadol does not leave the Mikdash. Lag BaOmer, hod shebehod, is the Kodesh HaKodashim; he brings the Mishnah of the ten miracles and the Gemara that the place of the Aron took no space, and explains that time, space and arithmetic are earthly limits that do not apply there.

title.en: Rashbi, the Kohen Gadol after the churban

summary.en: Mentioning the Gemara in Yoma, the Rav concludes that the Kodesh HaKodashim is above time, place and nature, and brings the Bnei Yissaschar that the joy of Lag BaOmer is above nature. After the churban there is still a Kohen Gadol who enters the Kodesh HaKodashim: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who revealed the hidden Torah, as the song Bar Yochai says.

title.en: Every Jew is a letter in the Sefer Torah

summary.en: The Rav asks why Rabbi Akiva's students, one of whom may truly have known more than his chavrusa, should have shown honor. He answers that, as there are 600,000 letters in the Torah and 600,000 souls, every Jew has a point no one else can replace, in which he surpasses even a great tzaddik; so a talmid chacham must honor even a simple Jew.

title.en: Words, families and kehillos: not mixing sedras

summary.en: The Rav extends the parable: letters form words, which are families, and lines, columns and sedras are neighborhoods and kehillos. He brings the Magen Avraham that a sedra may not be read on a Shabbos that is not its own, compares this to each kehillah keeping its minhagim, and notes that at certain times sedras are combined.

title.en: What includes all: Shabbos, Rashbi, the Beis HaMikdash

summary.en: The Rav contrasts the twelve tribes and months with the seven shepherds who include all of Klal Yisrael, the sea split into twelve at Krias Yam Suf and into seven in the future, and Rosh Chodesh fused with Shabbos. Rashbi, the Shabbos of the year, and the Beis HaMikdash include everything; the Beis HaMikdash was lost through sinas chinam, and the root of the divisions in Klal Yisrael is Yehudah and Yosef.

title.en: Combining sedras in seasons of achdus

summary.en: The Rav explains that in times when redemption is expected a breach of achdus is graver, so in four seasons (before Rosh Chodesh Nissan, the three weeks, Sefirah and before Rosh Hashanah) sedras are combined. He hints that the split of Yosef and Yehudah corresponds to Misnagdim and Chassidim, and illustrates it with the question whether a rav gets shishi or shlishi.

title.en: The sea's claim: shlishi against shishi

summary.en: The Rav brings the Midrash that the sea refused to split for Moshe, since it was created on the third day and man on the sixth, and Hashem rebuked it: at the redemption shishi and shlishi combine. The students of Rabbi Akiva did not see that each friend is superior in some hidden way; Rashbi, the Kohen Gadol of hod shebehod, revealed that every Jew has such a side, and so honor is due.

title.en: Melachah, curse and the sensitivity of Sefirah

summary.en: The Rav brings that Adam in Gan Eden did no melachah and that the 39 melachos come from the 39 curses, so on Shabbos, a day of blessing, melachah strikes at its essence. Likewise sinas chinam is worse in Sefirah, the walk toward the yovel of Shavuos and achdus; on Lag BaOmer Rashbi revealed the secret of each letter and soul, so the mourning stopped, as a Kohen Gadol has no mourning.

title.en: No mourning in Meron

summary.en: The Rav tells that the Satmar Rav, in Meron during the nine days, sang Bar Yochai since there is no mourning there, and brings from the writings of the Arizal the story of Rav Avraham HaLevi, punished for saying Nachem in Meron. From Meron the joy spreads, and he completes the Bnei Yissaschar's words: Rashbi reveals that even the lowest Jew carries a hidden point precious to Hashem.

title.en: Purim, Lag BaOmer and the point of the yud

summary.en: The Rav maps the festivals onto the middos and shows that Purim is also hod, so even the lowest Jew rejoices on it, and that Lag BaOmer always falls on Purim's day of the week. Both are a mystery; counting the letters of Baruch Shem and then Shema, the 33rd letter is the first yud of Hashem's name, the point that contains everything, and he closes that what he grasps of Lag BaOmer is only that it is a secret.
